Newsmax reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $54.1 million (up 16.5% YoY) and achieved its first quarterly net income as a public company at $2.9 million ($0.02/share). Gross margin expanded significantly to 43.1%, driven by high-margin affiliate fees which grew 81.9% and international licensing revenue surging from $0.7M to $4.6M in the quarter. Management reiterated full-year FY26 guidance of $212-$216 million, citing structural growth led by these expanding streams.

WidePoint reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $38 million (up from $37.3M YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $66k ($0.01 EPS) compared to a prior year loss of $618k, driven by growth in carrier services but offset by lower billable fees due to partial DHS shutdowns. Management highlighted the awarding of CWMS 3.0 and SEWP VI contracts as major wins for future scale while noting that Q2 results were impacted by non-recurring items and a temporary government shutdown.

Nektar Therapeutics reported Q2 FY26 non-cash royalty revenue of $10.1 million and a net loss of $40.6 million ($1.23 per share). Management raised full-year cash guidance to end at approximately $815-$840 million, extending the runway into late 2028 past mid-2028 data readouts. The company initiated its Phase III ZENITH AD program in July and received FDA alignment for a single registrational study (ZENITH AA) in alopecia areata to be initiated in early 2027.

Westwater Resources reported a Q2 FY2026 consolidated net loss of $4.3 million ($0.03/share), an increase from the prior year's loss of $3.9 million due to higher permitting costs, stock-based compensation, and product development expenses. The company received a significant non-dilutive milestone in the form of a formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan dedicated exclusively to advancing Phase I construction at the Kellyton Graphite Plant. Management maintains a target timeline for commercial production starting as soon as next year (late 2026/early 2027), contingent on securing remaining capital and closing documentation.

Wolverine World Wide reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $506 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.40 (up 14%), both exceeding expectations with the latter beating the upper end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.98B-$2.0B from $1.965B-$1.985B and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55-$1.65 from $1.43-$1.58, citing strong H1 execution by Merrell (up 10%) and Saucony (up 9%). The company also raised its full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 46.9%.

Fiscal Q4 FY26 revenues were $196.3 million, up 27% year-over-year driven by a more than doubling of concerts at The Garden and shared revenue from the Knicks' NBA championship run (a $7.4M increase in quarter). Adjusted operating income swung to an $18.6 million profit from a loss in the prior period. Management raised fiscal 2027 guidance expectations, citing strong demand momentum for events across venues.

Q3 same-store sales decreased 1.1% driven by a decline in transactions and polarizing Hot Ones promotion performance, partially offset by menu price increases. Restaurant level margin contracted to 17.6%, pressured by elevated beef costs (commodity inflation of 5.4%) and lower franchise revenue due to closures. Management lowered full-year guidance for restaurant count to approximately 2,100 units and adjusted franchise-level margin expectations downward.

WeRide reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 232 million, representing an 82% year-over-year increase and a 103% quarter-over-quarter surge driven by rapid scaling in overseas Robotaxi operations (up 47%) and L2+/L3 ADAS deployments. Gross margins expanded significantly to 37.5%, up from 28.1% last year, while operating leverage emerged as R&D expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue. Management raised guidance for cumulative vehicle installations in the L2++/L3 business, projecting over 100,000 units by year-end and exceeding 500,000 cumulatively next year.

WhiteFiber reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $28.8 million, a 54% year-over-year increase driven by cloud services growth to $23.8 million and colocation ramping at MTL-3. The company achieved positive Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million despite a net loss of $15 million due to higher depreciation on infrastructure expansion. Management highlighted significant progress in securing long-term contracts, including new multi-year agreements with Baseten ($165M value) and Prime Intellect ($108M value), while noting that the NC-1 site has commenced initial billing for its first tranche of capacity.

ERock reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $39.9 million (up 26% sequentially) and a net loss of $67.7 million driven by non-recurring IPO-related debt extinguishment losses totaling $48.8 million, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA miss relative to the prior quarter's -$12.4M as guidance was not yet issued at that time but implied positive H2 2026. Management provided full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $435-$465 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3-$9 million, projecting a return to profitability in the second half driven by backlog conversion.

Net revenue grew 2.5% to $499 million while adjusted comparable store sales increased 2.2%, driven by a 7.1% average ticket expansion that offset a 4.9% decline in traffic. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% and adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 per share, though management narrowed the full-year top-line guidance range due to persistent deferrals from lower-value transactions following an e-commerce re-platform.

Journey Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.5 million, a 23% year-over-year increase driven by Emrosi net product revenues of $8.1 million and improved ASPs. The company achieved positive GAAP EBITDA ($1.4M) and adjusted EBITDA ($2.9M), narrowing its loss to $0.01 per share compared to a prior period loss of $3.8M. Management highlighted accelerating prescription growth for Emrosi (up 20% sequentially) but noted that SG&A expenses remained elevated due to launch-related spending and upcoming marketing programs, with no specific guidance raised.

Forward Industries reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $10.8 million (up from $2.5M prior year) and a gross margin expansion to 62.2%, though the quarter included significant unrealized losses on digital assets totaling $49.8 million resulting in a net loss of $69.0 million ($0.8/share). Management highlighted strong operational execution with SOL per share growing 36% annualized, index inclusion into Russell indices, and successful deployment of capital via ATM issuances and buybacks to accrete value.

Phoenix New Media reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 216.7 million, a 15.8% year-over-year increase driven by paid services growth (RMB 69.8 million) and net advertising revenues of RMB 146.9 million. Gross margin expanded significantly to 57.3%, while operating expenses rose 30.4% due to digital reading initiatives, resulting in a narrow loss from operations but an improved net income attributable to the company compared to the prior year's loss. Management provided Q3 guidance of RMB 220.9 million to RMB 235.9 million total revenue and noted that while advertising demand was mixed due to contract timing issues, they see a structural shift toward content-driven monetization.

Franco-Nevada reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $348 million (implied by context) with adjusted net income and EPS up 46% year-over-year driven by record gold prices (+38%) and higher production at Antamina, South Arturo, Côté Gold, Casa Berardi, and Valentine. The company sold 132,405 total GEOs (up 18%), tracking toward the upper half of its full-year guidance range of 510,000-570,000 units despite a slight pullback in precious metal prices from Q1 highs.

Enovix reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $9 million (up 21% YoY), which landed at the high end of guidance but missed analyst consensus expectations due to a lack of specific beat confirmation in the text. The company recorded its first smart eyewear product revenue and advanced smartphone qualification milestones, though gross margins were pressured by South Korea mix shifts resulting in GAAP margins of 14.4%. Management maintained Q3 revenue guidance between $9-10 million but did not raise it despite strong pipeline growth.

Fossil Group reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $211 million (a 4% decline YoY) and gross margins expanding to 62.4%. Management raised full-year guidance for worldwide net sales to a 3%-5% decline range from the prior 4%-6%, while also raising adjusted operating margin expectations to 4%-6%.

Third quarter sales declined 8.4% year-over-year to $458.5 million due to softer demand and the closure of 80 stores, while adjusted EBITDA fell significantly from $81.6 million in Q3 FY2025 to $55.7 million. Gross margin contracted by roughly 3 percentage points (from 39.6% to 36.5%) driven by product mix shifts and higher distribution costs. Management withdrew previously issued full-year guidance for sales and adjusted EBITDA, citing lower-than-anticipated customer traffic during the peak season.

Fervo Energy reported a Q2 FY2026 operating loss of $28.7 million and net loss of $55.9 million as it ramps up construction at Cape Station with capital expenditures reaching $226.5 million in the quarter. Management provided non-GAAP revenue guidance for 2027 between $60 million and $80 million, explicitly noting this range is wider than usual due to potential curtailment events during initial commercial operations that are outside their control. While pipeline progress remains strong with significant capacity moved into advanced development and a record-breaking drilling pace demonstrated by the Sawtooth 7 well, immediate financial performance reflects pre-revenue burn.

Global-E reported Q2 FY26 results with GMV of $2.1 billion (up 44% YoY) and revenue of $299 million (up 39% YoY), significantly beating the high end of prior guidance. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for GMV, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA to reflect strong momentum from new brand launches, Managed Markets V2 adoption, and the recently closed acquisition of Passport. Adjusted EBITDA reached $62.4 million (a margin of ~21%), representing a more than 300 bps expansion compared to Q2 FY25.

Revenue increased 1% to $1.19 billion while comparable store sales declined 30 basis points due to Easter timing and a Cyclospora outbreak headwind expected in Q3. Adjusted EPS of $0.20 beat the outlook, driven by gross margin expansion to 30.2% from lower promotional spending despite flat gross profit dollars. Management raised full-year net sales guidance slightly but maintained comparable store sales expectations near zero.

T1 Energy reported Q2 FY2026 production of 935 MW at G1 Dallas and gross margins expanding to 19.5%, driven by higher throughput and favorable mix under fixed-margin contracts. Management raised the full-year 2026 guidance range, now expecting production near the high end of their previously stated 3.1-4.2 GW target. The company executed a $120 million convertible note private placement to bridge financing for G2 Austin construction while maintaining confidence in closing a comprehensive debt-based solution.

Harmonic reported Q2 FY26 broadband revenue of $133.5 million (up 54% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance ($115M-$125M) and EPS of $0.21, which beat the range of $0.15-$0.19. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a new range of $505 million to $525 million (up from prior $475M-$495M), citing record backlog and strong rest-of-market growth. The company completed its transformation into a pure-play broadband entity following the sale of its video business.

Commercial sales for the quarter were $0.4 million compared to $0.1 million in Q2 FY2025, while six-month commercial sales reached $0.9 million versus $0.2 million last year due to a rebuilding of the commercial team and inventory write-downs totaling $2.3 million over the half-year. The company reported a net loss of $36.8 million for Q2 FY2026, driven by non-cash remeasurement of contingent earnout liabilities rather than operational cash burn which remained positive at $29.4 million in H1. Management provided no updated financial guidance but reaffirmed the plan to file a supplemental BLA for dialysis access in November 2026 with an anticipated launch target in Q2 FY2027.

Hyliion reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.9 million and a net loss of $13.9 million, driven by increased R&D services work for the U.S. Navy. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $10-$15 million to approximately $15 million following the award of a new $41.7 million military contract and faster-than-expected ramp-up on existing programs.

IceCure Medical reported first-half FY2026 revenue of $1.8 million, representing a 45% year-over-year increase driven by higher sales of ProSense systems and disposable probes. Gross margin expanded to 30%, though this was partially offset by foreign exchange fluctuations compared to the prior period's 28%. The company ended with approximately $12 million in cash following financing activities.

Energous reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 million (up from ~$1M prior year) and a gross margin of 19% for the six months ended June 30, which was below recent levels due to temporary U.S.-based capacity retooling costs and higher-priced alternative component sourcing. Management explicitly declined to provide specific revenue guidance but emphasized that Q2 margins were depressed by strategic decisions to prioritize customer delivery timelines over short-term profitability. The company highlighted strong pipeline expansion with Fortune 10 customers, a new FCC certification for the PowerBridge Pro+, and an end-to-end solution launch expected in H2.

Valens Semiconductor reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.1 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($17.2M-$17.6M) and beating prior quarter results. GAAP gross margin was 61.5%, within the guided range but down from Q1 due to automotive testing expenses which are expected to stabilize in future quarters. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $78 million - $81 million, up from the previous range of $75 million-$77 million.

Infleqtion reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $12.6 million, representing an 116% year-over-year increase driven by organic growth in quantum computing and sensing. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $43 million from prior expectations. Management highlighted significant government validation including a Department of Commerce letter of intent for up to $100 million, three Genesis Mission projects with the DOE, and delivery of the UK's first operational neutral atom quantum computer.

Avino reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $26.8 million and net income of $10.9 million ($0.06/share), beating the prior year's EPS but missing on silver production due to a strategic decision to mine lower-grade surface material at Avino Mine which reduced ounces sold by approximately 5,000 oz compared to Q1. Management highlighted an inaugural mineral reserve estimate of 127M silver-equivalent ounces and record cash balances of $144 million, while noting that current costs are elevated due to processing development ore rather than production-grade material.

Applied Aerospace & Defense reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $167.3 million (up 47% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $36.4 million following its IPO. Management raised full-year guidance to a range of $670-$690M in revenue, citing strong backlog conversion and second-half volume ramps. The quarter was impacted by one-time share-based compensation from the accelerated vesting at IPO.

Adecoagro reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $173 million and gross sales of $535 million; while the fertilizer segment drove record earnings with higher volumes and prices, results in sugar/ethanol were softer due to lower sugar prices/volumes and a strategic decision to hold ethanol inventories. Management raised full-year guidance for fertilizers above initial projections but maintained caution on other segments citing inventory strategies and market volatility.

American Integrity Insurance Group reported record Q2 FY2026 results with gross premiums written increasing 13.8% to $327 million and income before taxes reaching a company-record $46.4 million. The quarter featured significant growth in voluntary new business, particularly in Tri-County (up 40x YoY) and middle-aged homes segments, alongside successful reinsurance renewal economics with rate reductions of 15%-20%. Management raised the outlook for investment income following a post-quarter deployment of $200 million into fixed-income securities.

Allogene provided a business update for Q2 FY2026 focusing on clinical progress rather than financial results, highlighting the receipt of RMAT and Fast Track designations for cema-cel in first-line consolidation based on interim MRD data. The company reported accelerating enrollment to reach its goal of 100 active sites by year-end but maintained guidance that the primary EFS analysis will occur mid-2027 without raising expectations despite faster site activation.

Allot reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $27.7 million (up 15% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.09, driven by a 47% increase in Security-as-a-Service revenue to $9.4 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from the previous range of $113M-$117M to $115M-$118M and narrowed it due to accelerating order momentum, particularly in North America where recurring revenues now represent two-thirds of total sales.

Altimmune reported Q2 FY2026 results that were in line with expectations, posting a net loss of $22.8 million ($0.12/share) compared to the prior year's loss of $22.1 million ($0.27/share). The company highlighted significant clinical progress including positive top-line data from the RECLAIM phase II trial for Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD), which met its primary endpoint and secondary registrational endpoints, and announced patient enrollment in the PERFORMA phase III MASH trial. Management expressed strong confidence in pemvidutide's differentiated profile across liver diseases while noting that financial results were neutral relative to guidance.

The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $217.7 million, beating the prior guidance range of $190M-$205M by approximately 10% and exceeding expectations with a 23.7% year-over-year increase driven primarily by organic growth of 20.5%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at roughly $46 million (up ~55%), while management reaffirmed full-year FY26 revenue guidance of $980M-$1B despite acknowledging that the pace of M&A deal closures is slower than anticipated, resulting in lower-than-planned inorganic contribution. Management expressed strong confidence in organic momentum and pricing power but noted ongoing investments in Global Mobility and consulting which currently suppress margins.

Annexon reported Q2 FY2026 financial results and announced a strategic expansion of its ARCHER II phase III trial for vonaprument in geographic atrophy by adding an independent month 24 dual primary endpoint alongside the existing month 15 readout. Management expressed strong confidence that the study will meet or exceed targets at both time points, citing robust patient retention (discontinuation rate <10%) and dosing compliance (>95%). The company also confirmed it is on track to submit a BLA for its GBS drug candidate tanruprubart in Q4 2026 following positive initial FORWARD study data.

Aquestive reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $13.8 million (up from $10M in the prior year quarter) and a net loss of $22.9 million ($0.18/share), driven by an $11.7 million one-time debt extinguishment charge on its 13.5% notes. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of $46-$50 million but reiterated that the Anaphylm resubmission will be a standard six-month review, with no specific date raised despite positive human factors and PK data supporting the filing in Q3.

Atea Pharmaceuticals reported positive top-line results for its Phase III C-BEYOND trial in Q2 FY2026, demonstrating statistical non-inferiority to the standard of care EPCLUSA with an SVR rate of 93.9% versus 94.8%. The company has $219.5 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, providing a runway anticipated through 2027 while R&D expenses increased due to Phase III advancement.

The company reported Q2 revenue of $24 million (a 127% YoY increase) and Adjusted EBITDA of $17.4 million (up nearly 100%), driven by record GEO sales at the higher end of guidance. Management stated they are tracking towards the upper end of their annual GEO guidance range, with cash flow supporting a maiden dividend and share repurchases while preparing for the Vizsla acquisition closing in Q3.

Consolidated revenue declined approximately 9.6% year-over-year to $44.1 million due to significant pressure in national and local agency channels (down ~21% and ~12%, respectively), though local direct revenue grew by 9%. Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially from a Q1 loss of negative $0.4 million to positive $5.3 million, driven largely by the completion of a debt restructuring that generated a gain on debt of approximately $91.8 million and reduced interest expense.

BETA Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $14.7 million, significantly beating the guidance range of $8-$11 million and showing year-over-year growth of 146%. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to a new high-end range of $42-$50 million following strong execution on eIPP operations, charger deliveries, and defense programs like EPFD. Adjusted EBITDA was -$110 million, landing at the midpoint of the guided range.

Boyd Group Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1 billion (up 30% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 45%, driven by a new location footprint expansion and same-store sales growth of 2.9%. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 13.4%, reflecting accelerated synergy realization from the Joe Hudson's acquisition, leading management to raise their full-year synergy target to $35 million.

Q2 adjusted EBITDA declined $44.7 million to $43.8 million due to startup costs for the Odin rig ($11.1M increase), higher fuel/insurance expenses from Middle East conflict ($7.3M increase), and a credit loss provision of $10.8 million, resulting in a net loss of $241.4 million. Management expects Q3 adjusted EBITDA to improve significantly as six transitioning rigs resume operations alongside the Odin commencing work, targeting an average fleet size of 23 active rigs for the quarter.

BitGo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43 million (up 14.7% sequentially and 79.6% YoY), but GAAP net loss narrowed to $19M from a prior quarter's $60.7M due to lower unrealized mark-to-market losses on digital assets ($18.8M vs $53.7M in Q1) rather than operational profitability improvements. Management explicitly stated that financial performance fell short of expectations, citing lower margins and an unfavorable revenue mix driven by reduced spot trading spreads and a large institutional staking client operating at a significantly lower take rate (6% vs 10% YoY). The company raised its cost base reduction initiatives to $21M in annualized savings starting Q3 following workforce reductions.

Cerebras Systems reported Q2 FY26 core revenue of $209.9 million (up 103% YoY) and record gross margins at 40.6%, beating guidance on all metrics despite a sequential margin dip due to temporary rented capacity costs for OpenAI ramp-up. Management raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to the range of $880-$890 million, along with adjusted gross and operating margin targets. The company highlighted significant progress in securing over 600 MW of data center capacity by end-2027 and expanding manufacturing capabilities.

Central Puerto reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $145 million and revenues of $453.3 million, representing significant growth driven by self-procured fuel margins and seasonal spot prices. Management raised guidance for battery storage projects to contribute between $25-27 million in 2027 once operational. The company maintains a healthy net leverage ratio of 1.2x while advancing commercial contracting efforts.

CuriosityStream reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $23.2 million (up 22% YoY) and record Adjusted EBITDA of $11.4 million with a gross margin expansion to 73%. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $77-$82 million and H2 adjusted EBITDA between $6-$10 million, noting the latter reflects a conservative approach rather than anticipated headwinds.

Titan Mining reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of $25.7 million (up 57% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.6 million. The company reaffirmed full-year zinc guidance for production between 62-66 million payable pounds, noting that current cost performance is ahead of the annual run rate due to recovering from a Q1 outage. Management highlighted significant commercial progress in graphite with two new customer agreements and confirmed district-wide germanium enrichment.

IFS reported Q2 FY2026 net income of PEN 585 million and ROE of 18.5%, representing a decline from the prior quarter due to normalizing investment results and cost of risk following an exceptionally strong first quarter, though earnings recovered 23% year-over-year. Revenues increased 9% year-over-year but declined slightly quarter-over-quarter as funding costs rose 20 bps and yield on assets fell 10 bps. Management maintained full-year ROE guidance above 17% while expressing caution regarding potential El Niño impacts in the second half of the year.

Inovio reported a net loss of $6 million ($0.07 per share) for Q2 FY2026 compared to a prior year loss of $23.5 million, driven by non-cash warrant liability gains rather than operational performance issues. The company raised approximately $18.3 million in July 2026 via an equity offering and expects its cash runway to extend into late Q1 FY2027 through the anticipated PDUFA date of October 30 for INO-3107. Management confirmed that FDA inspections are complete with only one observation addressed, but noted they cannot comment on accelerated approval eligibility until after label negotiations begin in September.

PFG reported Q4 FY26 net sales growth of 6.4% and adjusted EBITDA increasing 7.4%, with full-year revenue up nearly 9%. Management raised guidance for fiscal 2027 to $72.5B-$73B in sales (midpoint +7.2%) and $2.125B-$2.225B adjusted EBITDA, citing momentum from new accounts like Love's Travel Stops & RaceTrac and procurement synergies.

Integra Resources reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $70.8 million and adjusted EPS of $0.06 per share, representing a beat on the prior year's earnings while maintaining full-year production guidance at 70k-75k oz despite higher costs. The company maintained its AISC guidance range but raised total cash cost guidance to reflect increased royalties from strong gold prices and higher fuel/explosive expenses. Management highlighted record throughput of 87,867 tons per day and a significant increase in ore placed on heap leach pads.

Nexxen reported record Q2 results with programmatic revenue of $95.2 million (up 12% YoY) and contribution ex-TAC of $97.8 million (up 11% YoY). The company raised its full-year guidance for both contribution ex-TAC ($388M-$402M, up from prior midpoint) and programmatic revenue ($380M-$393M, up from prior midpoint), marking the first top-line guide raise of the year. Management highlighted record CTV revenue growth of 33% YoY to $37.8 million and strong enterprise spend increases.

Octave reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $398 million, down 1% organically due to a shift toward recurring models and timing delays in public safety perpetual deals totaling approximately $5 million that slipped into the next year. Adjusted operating margin was 29%, slightly lower than the prior year's 31% primarily driven by incremental public company launch costs (listing/audit fees) and reduced R&D capitalization of roughly 7%. Management lowered full-year total revenue guidance to a range reflecting these deal timing uncertainties, while reiterating ARR growth targets.

Omeros reported Q2 FY26 results driven by its first full quarter of YARTEMLEA sales, generating $32.2 million in gross revenue and $4.1 million in positive operating cash flow while repurchasing shares and convertible notes to strengthen capital structure. Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance for the third quarter or beyond due to a need to gain additional experience with prescribing trends and market dynamics following the launch. The company noted that reported GAAP net income was significantly impacted by non-cash mark-to-market adjustments on its 2029 convertible notes, which excluded from adjusted results showing an $1.8 million loss.

The company reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $12.9 million and a net loss of $6.2 million, missing expectations due to customer-directed delays in processing Hanford waste streams that shifted recognition into the second half. Despite the financial miss, management highlighted significant forward progress including a new master IDIQ award for tank waste operations with a maximum value of approximately $4.4 billion and backlog growth of 29% year-over-year. Management expressed confidence in H2 guidance driven by anticipated ramp-up from DFLAW facilities starting Q3 and permit expansions expected to be ready by the third quarter of 2027.

Protalix reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $19.9 million and net income of $3.8 million ($0.05 per share), driven by a $4.4 million increase in Elfabrio sales to Chiesi partially offset by lower Pfizer sales. Management stated that positive revenue trends keep the company firmly on track with its full year 2026 guidance, which remains unchanged from prior periods.

PolyPid reported a net loss of $7.8 million ($0.35 per share) for Q2 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $10 million loss driven by reduced G&A expenses following option vesting and secured partnership milestones. The company highlighted transformative regulatory progress with FDA acceptance of its NDA for D-PLEX100 ahead of schedule without filing review issues, alongside a priority review designation setting a PDUFA goal date of November 28, 2026. Financially strengthened by $30 million in upfront and near-term milestones from the Azurity partnership (totaling $45 million including post-signing payments), management expects existing cash resources to fund operations into 2028.

RADCOM reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $11.8 million, a decline of 33% year-over-year compared to $17.7 million in the prior period, driven by customer deployment delays due to rising server infrastructure costs rather than demand weakness or competitive loss. Management reaffirmed its revised full-year 2026 guidance range of $57-$63 million (midpoint $60M) and announced a new share repurchase program of $20-25 million, while noting that deployment activity is expected to normalize in Q1 FY27.

Resideo reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of just under $2 billion (up ~2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $249 million (up 19% YoY), exceeding the high end of prior guidance. Management provided a standalone full-year 2026 outlook with revenue between $2.9B-$2.95B, which represents a lower growth rate than previously implied for the combined entity due to the ADI spin-off and specific headwinds in the OEM security channel.

Red Robin reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $278 million (down from prior year) with comp sales up 1.3% driven by a 1.5% average check increase offsetting flat traffic and the expiration impact of value promotions. Restaurant-level operating margin expanded to 14.7%, while management maintained full-year guidance despite missing revenue expectations due to restaurant closures and promotional headwinds.

Coherent reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $2.05 billion (up 34% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 (up 74% YoY), driven by exceptional demand in data center transceivers, OCS, and CPO ramping ahead of schedule. Management raised Q1 FY27 guidance to revenue between $2.2B-$2.4B with a non-GAAP EPS range of $1.85-$2.05, citing record bookings extending into 2028 and accelerated capacity expansion on the six-inch indium phosphide platform.

Riskified reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $98.7 million (up 22% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.9 million (an 84% increase). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($405M midpoint, up from prior range) and adjusted EBITDA ($36M midpoint), citing accelerated growth driven by Digital Finance expansion and live sports events.

Q2 revenues increased 13% sequentially and 50% year-over-year to an annualized run rate of $46 million (up from Q1's $39.4M), driven by new campus openings in Miami-Opa Locka Phase II, Dallas, Phoenix, Denver, and Addison. Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at approximately -$0.9 million for the quarter but is expected to turn positive upon opening of Bradley and Addison Phase II later this year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with an annualized revenue run rate between $42M-$46M and adjusted EBITDA between $4M-$6M.

Cisco reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $17.3 billion (up 18% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%, driven by strong networking orders up 35%. The company exceeded the high end of its guidance for both the quarter and fiscal year, with full-year revenue reaching a record $63.3 billion. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to a range of $72.2-$73.4 billion (implying ~15% growth) and increased EPS guidance to $5.05-$5.11.

Standard Lithium reported a net loss of $3.1 million for Q2 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $5 million loss driven by higher cash balances and FX gains. The company successfully completed two major pre-FID milestones: securing construction contracts with Wood Group and S&B Engineers, and receiving a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) on its NEPA review for the Southwest Arkansas project. Management maintains an unchanged expectation to achieve Final Investment Decision later in 2026.

Similarweb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $77.2 million (up 9% YoY), exceeding the top end of guidance and delivering positive GAAP operating profit for the first time in company history with normalized free cash flow of $8.7 million. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $340-$380 million and non-GAAP operating profit guidance to $24-$26 million, citing strong enterprise demand and AI-driven data consumption as key drivers.

Virgin Galactic reported Q2 FY2026 with operating expenses of $65 million and capital expenditures of $41 million, resulting in free cash flow of -$91 million. Management raised the first commercial spaceflight to February 2027 due to modest time extensions on installation tasks but noted that a new tranche at higher price points was oversubscribed by over $50 million. The company expects quarterly positive cash flow within 2027 and projects adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1 billion annually with two fully utilized space ports.

Spire reported Q2 FY26 core revenue of $18 million, representing a 16% year-over-year increase and a 19% sequential gain driven by space services data delivery and increased RFGL purchases. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $75-$85 million (midpoint ~$80M), noting that over 85% of the midpoint is already under contract as of late July, despite a one-time gross margin contraction to 38% caused by the cancellation of the WildFireSat contract. The company highlighted progress on NOAA negotiations for an eight-figure microwave sounding opportunity and expects its Radio Occultation (RO) follow-on award in September to exceed last year's $11.2M annual value.

Spero Therapeutics reported no revenue for Q2 FY2026 compared to $14.2 million in the prior year period due to collaboration milestones being fully realized previously and a shift away from Pfizer/GSK funding sources. Net loss widened to $9.6 million (diluted EPS of -$0.16) driven by increased G&A expenses, though R&D costs decreased significantly following the early completion of the Utebzi Phase III trial in 2025.

Second quarter net sales were $93.5 million, representing an 111% year-over-year increase driven by strong performance in China and the U.S., while excluding a one-time order of $25.9 million recognized in Q3 2025 that will not repeat. The company returned to profitability with net income of $8.1 million ($0.16 per diluted share) compared to a loss last year, supported by gross margin expansion to 74.5%. Management highlighted the successful launch and adoption of EVO+ in China as well as back-to-back record quarters in the U.S., though they declined to provide specific numerical guidance for Q3 or full-year targets.

Brinker reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.536 billion with consolidated comp sales growth of +5% and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.07 (up from $2.49 last year). Management provided fiscal 2027 guidance for revenues between $6.15B-$6.27B and adjusted EPS between $12.60-$13.40, which represents a raise compared to prior expectations given the inclusion of an additional operating week in Q4. While Chili's delivered strong same-store sales growth driven by traffic and price, Maggiano's reported comp sales declines of -5.3% with flat profit assumptions built into next year.

Anterix reported Q1 FY2027 GAAP revenue of $2 million and operating expenses of $9.5 million, including an approximately $11 million gain from broadband license exchanges that significantly improved the income statement. Management highlighted a strong balance sheet with no debt and cash reserves exceeding $116 million while noting active engagement on nearly a dozen utility spectrum opportunities. The company reiterated it does not provide formal financial guidance but expects single-digit million gains in subsequent quarters.

Nebius Group reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $582 million (up 454% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $236 million with a margin expansion to 41%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for group revenue between $3 billion-$3.4 billion, annualized run-rate revenue of $7 billion-$9 billion, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 40%, citing strong momentum from new capacity additions and high-margin asset-light models.

Marex reported Q2 FY26 revenues of $696 million (up 39% YoY) and adjusted profit before tax of $166 million (up 56% YoY), driven by strong growth across clearing, agency/execution, market making, solutions, and NII. Management highlighted a diversified platform with structural growth offsetting cyclical volume declines in key exchanges, resulting in an expanded adjusted PBT margin to 24%. The company reaffirmed its ability to grow earnings resiliently through organic expansion and disciplined M&A.

Milestone Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY26 product revenue of $0.6 million and a net loss of $28.6 million ($0.21/share), driven by significant increases in SG&A expenses to $22.6 million due to commercial launch costs, while R&D decreased slightly to $3.5 million. Management highlighted that Q2 coverage was only 25% but noted meaningful progress post-quarter close pushing total covered lives past the 50% threshold for commercially insured patients. The company expects revenue per script and prescription volume to improve in H2 as co-pay mitigation decreases with broader formulary access.

The company reported a net loss of $8.5 million and an adjusted FFO loss of $1.6 million for the second quarter, representing significant improvement over last year's losses but still missing expectations for profitability. Management highlighted strong almond prices ($2.70/lb final pricing expected) which will drive revenue recognition in Q4 2026 following a down pistachio crop and disappointing water allocations that increased operating expenses.

Ituran reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $104.8 million (up 21% YoY) and net income of $17.3 million (up 29% YoY), driven by a recurring subscription base growing to $80 million. The company added 41,000 net new subscribers for a total of 2.711 million and generated record cash flow from operations of $32.2 million. Management declared a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share ($10M) and executed $3M in buybacks.

Jumia reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $52 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $8.7 million from a prior year loss of $13.6 million, driven by strong growth in lower-margin categories like fashion and home goods that offset supply disruptions in phones/electronics. Management maintained its full-year profitability guidance despite lowering the GMV outlook due to external headwinds including memory chip shortages, fuel surcharges, and demand pressure from falling cocoa prices in Ivory Coast.

KEPCO reported H1 FY26 revenue of KRW 46,317 billion (up 0.3% YoY) and net income of KRW 2,796.5 billion, driven by a 16.7% increase in other revenue but offset by power sales declining 0.4%. Management noted that while full-year nuclear contribution is expected to slightly rise due to Saeul Unit 3 additions, H1 capacity factors were weak and fuel costs rose 8.8%, leading to cautious guidance on tariff hikes for the remainder of the year.

Kornit reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $55.3 million (up 11.2% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with positive adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow for the 11th consecutive quarter. Management raised full-year growth expectations to 'high single-digit' from low single-digits, citing a structural shift in screen printing toward digital production where approximately 60% of system sales went to traditional printers. The company highlighted an increase in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by $7 million and noted that roughly 80% of total revenue is now recurring or highly recurring.

Second quarter revenue reached a record $9 million, representing more than 200% year-over-year growth driven by the Security Force acquisition and core subscriptions. Gross margin turned positive at approximately 7%, marking the second consecutive quarter of profitability following an accretive acquisition integration. Management reiterated that every subsequent quarter will be better than the last while noting no specific numerical guidance was provided for future periods.

Kontoor Brands reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.2 billion (high end of outlook) and adjusted EPS of $2.12 (36% YoY increase), driven by strong Helly Hansen performance (+19% pro forma growth in first half). Management raised the full-year 2026 guidance for both operating income ($413M-$420M vs prior $411M-$418M) and EPS ($5.25-$5.35 vs prior $5.15-$5.25), citing mid-single-digit growth expectations for the second half despite conservative retail inventory levels.

Kura Oncology reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $9.1 million from KOMZIFTI and collaboration revenue of $11.8 million versus a prior year period with no product sales; the company achieved majority share of new patient starts in its second full quarter despite being second to market, driven by 35% sequential growth in new patients and strong clinical data supporting combination strategies.

StubHub reported Q2 FY26 GMS of $3.1 billion (up 34% YoY) and revenue of $573 million (up 33%), driven by the World Cup but with gross margins compressed to ~82%. Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled year-over-year to approximately $106 million, expanding margin to 18%, while free cash flow reached a trailing twelve-month total of $598 million. Management raised full-year GMS guidance to $10.1-$10.3 billion (representing 10-12% growth) from the prior outlook of 8-10%, maintaining EBITDA guidance at $400-$420 million.

Alpha and Omega reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $170.4 million (down 3.5% YoY), with Non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 23.7%. While advanced computing grew strongly, the quarter was impacted by softness in traditional PC markets due to memory costs and a specific operational impact from Typhoon Dolphin flooding in Shanghai affecting packaging operations.

Usio reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of approximately 19% (excluding interest income approaching 20%), with total payment dollars and transactions up 27%. The company met or beat analyst expectations on the top line while generating positive GAAP net income for the second consecutive quarter. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of 14%-16%, upgrading from prior guidance of 10%-12%.

Syntec Optics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $8.3 million, a 26% year-over-year increase driven by growth across defense, space, AI infrastructure, and biomedical segments. Gross margin expanded to 26%, returning the company to positive operating income ($0.3M) after an operating loss in Q1 FY2025. Management raised full-year guidance expectations for sequential revenue growth in both Q3 (guidance $8.3M-$9.0M) and Q4 (guidance $8.75M-$9.25M).

Liftoff reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $220 million (up 35% YoY and 7% QoQ) with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 60%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue between $870M-$880M ($27-28% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $510M-$518M. The strong performance was driven by market expansion, Cortex self-learning, model breakthroughs, and specific demand from the FIFA World Cup.

Consolidated revenues reached $264.2 million in Q2 FY2026, representing a 5.1% year-over-year increase driven by advanced modality volumes growing 6.3%. Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $56.4 million compared to the prior year quarter due to incremental public company costs and stock-based compensation increases offsetting strong underlying volume growth. Management narrowed its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance range from $234M-$242M to $235M-$241M while maintaining revenue guidance at $1.045B-$1.097B.

Liquidia reported Q2 FY2026 net product sales of $170.4 million for YUTREPIA, representing a 31% quarter-over-quarter increase and over-tripling growth since launch initiation in June 2025. The company moved from a net loss to profitability with approximately $74.7 million in net income and $96.3 million in non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter, driven by strong patient starts exceeding 5,000 as of July 31. Management expressed confidence that YUTREPIA is capturing a growing share of the expanding inhaled prostacyclin market while maintaining its trajectory toward over $1 billion in net revenue for 2027.

Second quarter revenues reached $5.9 million, a significant sequential increase from Q1's $3.3 million driven by Smart Cart deliveries rising to $4.4 million (up from $2.5M). Gross margin expanded materially to 42.6% as the new Chinese manufacturing facility came online and production costs decreased. Management raised full-year delivery guidance, targeting at least 10,000 units delivered by year-end.

MaxCyte reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.3 million (down 15% YoY) and core revenue of $6.5 million (down 21% YoY), driven by lower license revenue from discontinued programs and a difficult comparison to accelerated PA purchases in the prior year quarter. Gross margin contracted to 77%, while operating expenses decreased significantly due to restructuring benefits, resulting in an improved net loss despite the top-line miss. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $30M-$32M total revenue with low single-digit growth expected for H2.

Second quarter revenue declined 30% year-over-year to $20.5 million due to a limited number of large customers and macroeconomic factors including MFN pricing dynamics, while adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million. Management reiterated full year 2026 guidance for revenue between $95-$100 million and adjusted EBITDA between $21-$25 million despite the miss on top-line growth. The company highlighted margin expansion to a normalized high 60%-low 70% range, debt paydown progress, and new product launches including DeepIntent integration.

NANO Nuclear reported a Q3 net loss of $10.1 million compared to $7.6 million in the prior year quarter and a YTD net loss of $25.8 million versus $32 million last year, driven by higher operating expenses as it scales engineering and regulatory workstreams for its UIUC project. The company ended with approximately $580 million in liquidity after raising roughly $26 million via ATM proceeds, though no revenue guidance was provided given the pre-revenue nature of the business. Management highlighted substantial progress on NRC licensing milestones (environmental assessment expected Q1 2027) and strategic partnerships but offered no specific commercial deployment timelines or financial targets.

Amcor reported Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS of $1.23 (up 23% YoY) and revenue of $6.4 billion, with full-year synergies reaching $285 million ahead of initial targets. Management provided a transition period outlook for the six months ending December 31st expecting adjusted EPS between $1.80-$1.90 per share. The company highlighted broad-based volume growth and successful integration progress despite macroeconomic headwinds.

Trimble reported Q2 FY26 organic revenue growth of 10% and EBITDA margins expanding to 28.6%, both beating the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year EPS guidance by $0.10 (to a midpoint implying ~$3.75) and revenue guidance by $50 million, citing strong momentum in AECO (+9%) and Field Systems (+12%). The company announced a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization while undertaking a strategic review of its Transportation business amid inbound interest.

PagSeguro reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of BRL 3.4 billion (up 2% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of BRL 2.06 (up 10% YoY), beating expectations but missing the top end of its full-year guidance range due to a challenging macro environment and elevated interest rates. Management maintained its full-year gross profit guidance despite headwinds, citing expected sequential improvements in financial costs during H2 as key drivers for meeting targets.

Vestis reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $662 million (down 1.8% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $81 million (up 23% YoY), driven by a return to positive Revenue Per Pound growth for the first time as a public company despite volume declines from exiting low-quality linen business. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance midpoint to $165 million, citing strong working capital execution and transformation benefits realized in Q4.

For the quarter ended June 30th, core net investment income per share was $0.26, exceeding the base dividend of $0.24 but missing analyst expectations due to an unrealized loss of $18.3 million driven by a write-down on non-accrual investments and equity positions. NAV declined approximately 2% from the prior quarter primarily attributable to this specific provision for losses rather than portfolio-wide deterioration, with PIK income remaining low at 2.4%. Management maintained a cautious tone regarding macro headwinds like tariffs affecting consumer names while highlighting resilience in government services.

Wrap Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.1 million, representing a 103% increase year-over-year and doubling compared to the prior quarter. Gross margin expanded significantly to approximately 75%, while net loss narrowed by 39% to $2.3 million due to non-recurring warrant liability losses in the prior period. Management maintained its full-year revenue growth guidance of approximately double, citing new market access from ATF declassification and federal funding returns.

NHI reported Q2 FY2026 results in line with expectations following the sale of its NHC portfolio for $560 million and a gain on property dispositions totaling approximately $137 million ($98.5M proceeds + $22M gain). While net income per share beat due to these one-time gains, core FFO metrics were flat or slightly down compared to the prior year period. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite same-store SHOP NOI growth being below the midpoint of their 1%-3% range in H1.

Sea reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.8 billion (up 48% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of over $917 million (up 11% YoY). Management reaffirmed full-year GMV growth guidance at around 25%, citing strong momentum in Shopee, Monee, and Garena across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Brazil, and other markets. The company highlighted significant unit economics improvements, particularly in logistics fulfillment and advertising take rates.

Stellus Capital reported Q2 FY2026 results with GAAP net investment income of $0.26 per share and core NII also at $0.26, resulting in a NAV increase driven by realized/unrealized gains rather than organic earnings growth. Management lowered the quarterly dividend to $0.25 due to reduced spillover cash balances but expects to return to higher distributions as income normalizes. The portfolio fair value decreased slightly from Q1 despite new investments and repayments, with asset quality noted as 'slightly below plan' due to elevated nonaccruals.

Rackspace reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $670 million (up 1% YoY), beating Private Cloud guidance but missing Public Cloud targets due to lower infrastructure/services demand; total company Non-GAAP gross margin contracted by 120 bps to 18.6%. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance at a decline, citing a strategic pivot away from low-margin Public Cloud toward higher-value AI and regulated enterprise services.

Red Violet reported a record Q2 FY2026 with revenue of $26.7 million (up 23% YoY), adjusted gross margin expanding to a new high of 86%, and cash flow from operations reaching $10.6 million. The company added a record 447 IDI customers in the quarter, including significant growth across four verticals while FOREWARN expanded into home healthcare with over 25,000 new users. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 'high 30s' following this exceptional performance.

QuickLogic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $5.5 million (up 48.7% YoY), which missed the midpoint of guidance due to a delayed contract extension and an uncertain commercial ASIC design targeting Intel 18A, leading management to narrow full-year growth outlook to 70%-80%. Management forecast flat Q3 revenue but raised confidence in securing new contracts for late-stage negotiations and government work. The company expects non-GAAP profitability and cash flow positive operations for the second half of FY26.

Quantinuum reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $8 million (up 279% YoY) and bookings of $4.3 million, with year-to-date bookings reaching approximately $81 million against a full-year guidance range of $28-$32 million for 2026. The company highlighted significant progress on its Sol system roadmap via Honeywell Aerospace validation and secured major strategic partnerships including an LOI from the U.S. Department of Commerce, agreements with Oracle and HPE, and new manufacturing alliances to scale supply chains. Management expressed high confidence in their technology leadership and commercial momentum despite acknowledging that quarterly results may remain volatile as they transition into a public company.

Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA of $35 million (up nearly $20M YoY) driven by a 50% increase in TCE rates to an average of $18,153/day. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.10 per share and ended the quarter with unrestricted cash of $105 million following asset sales. Management maintains a positive outlook for H2 2026 citing seasonal tailwinds from Arctic trades and continued demand momentum.

On Holding reported Q2 FY26 net sales of CHF 850 million (up 13.5% on a reported basis), driven by strong DTC growth but moderated wholesale performance in the Americas due to deliberate watch-in restraint. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA margin at 19.5%-20%, while raising gross margin expectations to 'at least' 65%. The company reiterated its commitment to premium positioning and disciplined execution, noting that lower Q3 growth is expected before a re-acceleration in H2.

Total revenue was $187 million but included a negative adjustment of $136 million for exiting rail contracts; excluding this, revenues were higher than the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA increased by over 20% to $34 million driven by Harsco Environmental and aftermarket volumes at Rail, though adjusted loss per share was $0.63 due to one-time exit charges of roughly $190 million in accrued liabilities. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite better-than-anticipated first-half performance, citing uncertainty from Middle East geopolitical pressures.

NRGV reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.4 million (up 104% YoY) and GAAP gross margin expanding to 31%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $270-$310 million from the prior $225-$300 million, citing strong backlog growth to roughly $2 billion. The company highlighted its largest-ever contract (1.25 GW) and improved liquidity with cash ending at $148 million.

NextNav reported a net loss of approximately $33.8 million for Q2 FY2026 due to a non-cash derivative liability loss of roughly $32 million and warrant exercise proceeds offset by debt extinguishment gains, resulting in no GAAP or adjusted EPS beat against implied breakeven expectations from the prior period's transformational narrative. Management provided no specific revenue guidance but highlighted significant financial restructuring including becoming debt-free with approximately $300 million in liquidity as of June 30th and converting all outstanding warrants to shares. The company emphasized steady progress on FCC regulatory milestones, a new partnership with Safran Electronics & Defense for terrestrial 5G PNT validation, and technical achievements like demonstrating ~20 ns timing accuracy.

NGS reported record Q2 FY26 results with rental revenue of $49.4 million (up ~25% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expanding to 61.1%. The company increased full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $103-$108M from the prior range of $92.5-$97.5M, driven by a Flatrock acquisition contribution that added roughly half a month in Q2 and contracted organic growth raising expectations for 2026 deployments.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $5.1 million (down from Q1's $6.7M), with GAAP gross margin improving to 22.6% driven by ESS mix and pricing discipline. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $30-35 million despite the sequential decline, citing a backlog extending into 2028 for drone cells.

NCMI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58.4 million (up 12.7% YoY) and adjusted OIBDA of $2.1 million (a three-fold increase), with results falling within the company's guidance range despite June headwinds from film mix shifts and FIFA World Cup budget reallocation. The CEO announced a definitive agreement to acquire Captivate, valuing it at an enterprise value of $275 million for approximately 48,000 combined digital screens across theaters, offices, and residential properties. Management stated they are pausing dividend payments and share repurchases pending the transaction's closing in H2 FY26.

Mineralys Therapeutics reported a net loss of $241.1 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $43.3 million in the prior year quarter, driven by a one-time $200 million upfront payment to Tanabe Pharma Corporation and increased R&D expenses totaling $221.4 million. The company ended the period with cash equivalents and investments of $661.4 million, sufficient to fund operations through 2028 while awaiting FDA approval for lorundrostat expected by December PDUFA date.

Middleby reported Q2 FY26 commercial foodservice revenue of $631 million with organic growth of 8.3%, driven by strength in ice and beverage platforms despite a total margin headwind of nearly 100 basis points from inflationary costs exceeding tariff refunds. Management raised full-year organic revenue guidance for the core business to 6%-8% (from prior expectations) while maintaining adjusted EPS guidance at $6.73-$6.89, citing momentum in QSR new product adoption and a pent-up replacement cycle.

Mistras Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $193 million (up 4.2% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million ($25.8m vs prior year). Gross margin expanded by 10 basis points to a non-GAAP level implied around 73-74%, while operating income surged 53.6%. Management raised full-year guidance ranges for revenue (up to $740-$755M) and adjusted EBITDA (up to $92-$95M), citing strength in aerospace/defense and infrastructure offsetting a flat-to-down outlook for oil & gas.

908 Devices reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.1 million (up 23% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 57%. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance range to $68-$70 million, citing strong execution on FTIR modernization, the new NIRLab acquisition integration, and a specific $6 million ProtectIR order. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by over half year-over-year.

Lightwave Logic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $33 million (up from $26M prior year) and a net loss widening to $6.6 million ($0.04/share). The company expanded its commercial pipeline with five Stage 3 customers, including one Fortune Global 500 firm moving into execution phase for scale-across transceivers. Management highlighted progress on foundry wafers expected in August but noted that revenue recognition remains contingent on future milestones and qualification.

LENZ reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $5.5 million ($1.7M product revenue) and a net loss per share of $1.02 on a net loss of $31.9 million, with no GAAP or adjusted EPS provided in the text. Management highlighted an over 45% month-over-month increase in July prescriptions driven by new telehealth initiatives and national TV advertising, but explicitly stated that Q2 results were 'modest' growth rather than a significant beat. Guidance for H2 remains focused on assessing patient persistence data to align capital allocation with demonstrated performance.

Legend Biotech reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $341 million (implied from context) with total revenue growing 52% year-over-year to reach a new milestone in profitability. Adjusted net income was $63 million, representing an adjusted EPS of $0.16 per diluted share compared to $0.03 last year. The company achieved its first quarter of company-wide profitability on both IFRS and adjusted bases.

Lithium Argentina reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $110 million (up 4% sequentially) and free cash flow from operations of $141 million driven by realized prices averaging around $19,500 per ton. The operation averaged 93-95% design capacity for the year with costs remaining under $6,000 per ton despite a planned shutdown impacting Q2 production volume. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of 35,000-40,000 tons and highlighted significant balance sheet strength following debt reductions to $142 million at the JV level.

Second quarter revenue was $167.3 million (up 15.6% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA was $18.7 million, with results coming in at the midpoint of guidance despite late June white space. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to a range of $176-$188 million ($182m midpoint), citing improved activity levels driven by WolfPack integration and seasonal normalization. The company announced a proactive $125 million backstop equity rights offering designed to reduce leverage, improve liquidity, and strengthen the balance sheet.

KBDC reported net investment income of $0.42 per share and EPS of $0.16 for Q2 FY2026, slightly below the prior quarter's NII but in line with expectations given a lower dividend coverage ratio relative to NAV decline. The company maintained its target debt-to-equity range at 1.17x while rotating out of broadly syndicated loans into higher-yielding private credit assets averaging 566 bps over SOFR. Management noted modest deal flow pickup and stable watch list levels, though realized losses from Sundance and unrealized marks on specific positions weighed on NAV.

Seer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 million, a decrease from the prior year's $4.1 million and an increase sequentially from Q1's $2.8 million due to macroeconomic headwinds in academic funding and elongated sales cycles. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range of $16-$18 million despite the challenging environment, citing positive trends in customer interest for H2 driven by new commercial leadership and upcoming data releases.

Smithfield Foods reported record second quarter adjusted operating profit of $300 million and diluted EPS of $0.62, though consolidated sales declined 2.3% year-over-year to $3.7 billion due to volume pressure in fresh pork and packaged meats. Management updated its full-year outlook downward for total company adjusted operating profit (now expected between $1.225B-$1.375B) and sales guidance, citing softer commodity market assumptions and a cautious consumer environment.

Second quarter revenue of $233.5 million beat consensus estimates but adjusted EBITDA missed at $40.2 million due to a decline in commercial sheet door demand and lower margins driven by product mix. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting organic North America self-storage revenues down high single digits and adjusting Kiwi II Construction revenue expectations to reflect project delays.

Silvercorp reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of CAD 139 million (up 70% YoY) and net income of CAD 59.4 million, driven by a 135% increase in realized silver prices despite production declines at its Chinese operations due to safety upgrades. Management explicitly stated that full-year guidance is premature given the temporary shutdowns affecting Ying and GC mines, with current output running at only 40-50% of target for Q2.

Absci reported positive interim Phase I data for ABS-201 in the HEADLINE trial, demonstrating a favorable safety profile and an estimated half-life of at least 65 days supporting potential dosing two to three times over six months. The company announced a $40 million strategic investment from Eli Lilly alongside a completed $100 million financing round, bringing total cash reserves to approximately $201 million as of June 30, 2026. Management anticipates an interim proof-of-concept readout later in the year and plans to initiate a Phase II endometriosis trial in Q4.

OrganiGram reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of CAD 105.8 million (up 49% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 37%, driven by Sanity Group contributions which exceeded EUR 25M expectations for the full quarter. Adjusted EBITDA hit a new high of CAD 13.4 million, while Canadian share recovery in vapes and pre-rolls offset slightly lower domestic market share due to portfolio rationalization. Management raised guidance expecting revenue above CAD 350M for FY26 and meaningful margin expansion.

H&R Block reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $3.95 billion (up 4.9%) and adjusted EPS of $5.31 (up 13.9%), driven by higher net average charge, volume growth in assisted tax preparation, and momentum from Wave small business services. Management raised the full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to a range of $4.11 billion-$4.16 billion while maintaining adjusted EBITDA between $1.11 billion-$1.14 billion and raising the quarterly dividend by 10% to $0.46 per share.

Fourth quarter revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion and non-GAAP EPS was $3.23, significantly beating the high end of guidance due to strong components ($649M) and systems ($357M) performance driven by AI demand. Management raised Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance to a range of $1.225-$1.275 billion (midpoint $1.25B), noting they are hitting this target more than one quarter ahead of schedule, and projected non-GAAP operating margins between 39.5% and 40.5%. Gross margin expanded to 50.4%, crossing the previously targeted threshold at a much lower revenue run rate.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $17.7 million versus $17.1 million in the prior year, while gross margins expanded to a record 34.9% and adjusted EBITDA reached approximately 20%. Management attributes the lower-than-expected quarterly sales primarily to timing shifts of high-voltage deliveries into FY2027 due to supply chain constraints rather than lost business or demand deterioration.

Aramark reported Q3 FY26 organic revenue growth of 9% to $5 billion and adjusted operating income (AOI) expansion of nearly 20 basis points to a margin that drove AOI up 18%. Management raised the fiscal 2026 organic revenue guidance range from prior levels to an increase of 9%-10%, while reaffirming AOI growth expectations of 12%-17% and adjusted EPS growth of 20%-25%. The quarter was driven by record client retention at approximately 98%, strong new business wins totaling $1.6 billion year-to-date, and the initial ramp-up of Aramark Nexus operations.

Third quarter revenue of $3.5 billion came in slightly below expectations due to protest delays and low-margin material volume, though adjusted EBITDA hit a record $290 million with margins expanding to 8.3%. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($1.115B-$1.14B) and EPS ($2.40-$2.50), while maintaining free cash flow expectations, despite acknowledging a preliminary FY2027 revenue headwind of approximately 3% from NASA workforce directives.

AECOM reported Q3 FY2026 results impacted by a $337 million pre-tax charge related to delays in two Construction Management projects, causing NSR growth to fall below expectations despite strong wins and backlog increases. Adjusted EBITDA and EPS improved year-over-year excluding the charge but missed full guidance due to lower-than-expected revenue growth and cash burn from project completion costs. Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered for free cash flow (to $300 million) while maintaining adjusted earnings expectations, with a raised margin outlook driven by International segment performance.

YPF reported a record-breaking Q2 FY2026 with revenues of $6.6 billion (up 42% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA reaching $2.8 billion, marking the best quarter in company history. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to approximately $8 billion from a previous expectation of around $6 billion, driven by higher Brent price assumptions ($75/bbl vs prior $63). The company also increased its CapEx forecast range to $5.8-$6.2 billion and expects net leverage to decline significantly to nearly 1x.

Supermicro reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $11.1 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.70, both missing the company's own guidance due to customer delays in power readiness and cooling that pushed shipments into subsequent quarters. While gross margins expanded significantly to 17.6% (beating guidance) driven by favorable mix and one-time inventory/tariff benefits, management explicitly warned that Q4 results were not fully comparable year-over-year because of these timing shifts. The company raised its full fiscal year 2027 revenue outlook to a range of $65 billion-$72 billion despite the near-term shipment delays.

Venture Global reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $4.6 billion (up 48% YoY) and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 billion (a record high). Management raised full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance to a range of $8.7-$9.1 billion from the prior $8.2-$8.5 billion, citing strong execution and production at Calcasieu Pass despite summer seasonality. The company also increased its quarterly dividend by 122% to $0.04 per share.

Velo3D reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.7 million (up 52% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 21.5%. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from a range of $60M-$70M to $65M-$75M, citing strong demand in aerospace, defense, and energy sectors.

SINTX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $452,000 (up 199% YoY) and gross margins expanding to approximately 62%, driven by a shift from grant/contract work to product sales. However, the company incurred a net loss of $2.7 million with cash declining to $3.6 million due to significant working capital investment in inventory ($2.3M). Management provided Q3 guidance of $900k-$1.1M revenue but explicitly reiterated substantial doubt regarding its ability to continue as a going concern.

Ur-Energy reported Q2 FY2026 production of 141,000 pounds at Lost Creek and initial capture of 10,634 pounds at Shirley Basin, resulting in $14.4 million in sales revenue from contracted deliveries totaling 215,000 pounds. Management proactively deferred 300,000 pounds of 2026 deliveries to later years to manage ramp-up risk and maintain flexibility rather than providing specific volume guidance for the remainder of the year. While operational execution improved with sand filtration installation increasing flow rates at Lost Creek, the company explicitly stated it is not interested in spot sales and will prioritize inventory protection.

Second quarter revenue declined approximately 25% year-over-year to $7.9 million due to a roughly 52% drop in realized antimony prices despite higher volumes; gross margin compressed from 27% to 7%. Management lowered full-year guidance to $60-$75 million citing the significant decline in commodity pricing, while noting that DLA deliveries will begin recognizing revenue starting in Q3.

Taysha reported a net loss of $46.6 million ($0.13 per share) for Q2 FY2026 compared to a prior quarter's loss of $26.9 million, driven by increased R&D and G&A expenses related to BLA-enabling manufacturing initiatives and clinical trial expansion. The company completed dosing in the REVEAL pivotal (17 patients) and ASPIRE trials but disclosed one Grade 2 SAE involving peripheral sensory neuropathy requiring hospitalization for management, though recovery was rapid. Management maintains confidence in TSHA-102's efficacy data exceeding FDA thresholds while emphasizing a strengthened balance sheet with $455.4 million in cash to support operations through late 2028.

Q2 revenue was $15 million and GAAP net income was approximately $83.5 million, driven by a non-cash fair value gain of $82.8 million on Gram holdings rather than operational earnings power. Management raised the full run-rate OpEx savings from legacy Verb wind-downs to Q4 2026 due to transition costs and noted that staking yields are expected to evolve as the network matures, explicitly avoiding assumptions about indefinite current economics.

TME reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 8.9 billion (up 6% YoY) and net profit attributable to equity holders of RMB 2.5 billion (up from RMB 2.4 billion in the prior year). The quarter included approximately RMB 0.4 billion of revenues from Ximalaya consolidation, while gross margin declined slightly to 44.2% due to revenue mix shifts toward offline services and amortization impacts.

Grupo Supervielle returned to profitability in Q2 FY2026 with attributable net income of ARS 13 billion and adjusted net income of ARS 36 billion following a loss in the prior quarter. Management updated full-year guidance, lowering real loan growth expectations to 10%-15% from previously higher targets due to subdued retail demand, while raising NIM guidance to 17%-19%. The rightsizing program is largely complete with structural ROE reaching 14.4%, though management notes margin pressure in the second half as asset repricing begins.

Stereotaxis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.7 million, a year-over-year decline due to the lack of robotic system deliveries but an increase sequentially from Q1 driven by catheter sales. Gross margin was 58%, with operating loss widening slightly to $4.6 million compared to $4.0 million in the prior year quarter. Management provided specific guidance for recurring revenue growth ($7M in Q3, $8M in Q4) and system revenue stabilization at approximately $3M per quarter in H2, while explicitly stating that full-year visibility is limited by supply constraints on catheters.

Total revenue was $41.6 million, up 9% year-over-year driven by a 17% increase in Greenbrook to $26.9 million and double-digit growth in NeuroStar capital sales offsetting session declines. Gross margin expanded significantly to 61.1%, while the company reduced its cash burn from operations and investing to just $1.4 million compared to $3.8 million last year. Management narrowed full-year revenue guidance slightly but raised gross margin expectations, reflecting improved operational discipline.

Sable Offshore Corp reported Q2 FY2026 results where production ramped to 40,000 bpd but faced significant marketing constraints and a $30/bbl discount due to sulfur content and demurrage charges. Management completed the refinancing of the senior secured term note in July 2026 to retire seller financing, providing more flexibility despite not raising guidance for the back half of the year which includes elevated deducts. The company expects production constraints to alleviate by Q4 2026 with Platform Hondo coming online and a full 3P reserve report expected in Q1 2027.

Net revenue decreased to $19.7 million in Q2 FY26 from $22.2 million a year ago due to lower sales of ASA and ASE titles, while net loss improved significantly to $3 million primarily driven by the absence of an income tax provision recorded in the prior period. Management noted that major DLC launches scheduled for early July shifted revenue recognition into Q3 rather than Q2, resulting in fewer blockbuster releases during this quarter compared to historical norms.

Summit Midstream reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $60.7 million (a 12% increase vs Q1), driven by volume growth in Rockies and Mid-Con segments alongside a ~30% quarter-over-quarter rise in realized crude oil prices. Management tightened full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $235-$255 million while raising capital expenditure guidance to $100-$120 million, citing new well connections and Double E expansion projects.

JBS reported record net sales of $24 billion in Q2 FY2026 with Adjusted EBITDA reaching $1.3-1.4 billion depending on accounting standards (5.3% GAAP margin). While the company delivered a solid quarter and raised its full-year cash flow guidance to $5.1 billion, profitability was significantly impacted by non-recurring items including bond tender costs ($172M) and antitrust settlements ($133M), resulting in a net loss of $102 million. Management highlighted strong demand resilience but noted challenging U.S. beef margins due to high cattle costs and warned that the second half leverage will likely finish slightly above their 2x-3x target.

NeuroPace reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $22.8 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted gross margin of 83.4%, slightly down from the prior year due to material costs but supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $99.5M-$101.5M, reflecting improved visibility into service revenue which is now expected at approximately $1 million for the full year versus a previous expectation of $500k. However, the company disclosed that its PMA supplement expansion into idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE) was not approvable in its current form due to FDA requests for additional clinical evidence regarding specific patient subgroups.

Infinity Natural Resources reported Q2 FY26 net production of 348 Mcfe/d (up 75% YoY) and adjusted EBITDAX of $115M, a company record driven by strong oil growth (+102%) and NGL realizations up 70%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for net production between 345-375 Mcfe/d and development capex of $450-$500M. The quarter highlighted operational efficiency gains, including a step change in drilling speed (+15%) and completion cost reductions ($/ft), alongside the integration of Antero assets.
