DPC Holdings reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $269 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $48 million (up 33%), driven by strong growth in Engine Products segments. Adjusted EPS was $0.05, representing a significant recovery from the prior year's loss as net income moved into profit. Management initiated full-year guidance for revenue between $1 billion-$1.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $182 million-$187 million.

Consolidated Water reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $32.9 million, a decrease from the prior quarter and year-over-year decline in manufacturing offset by growth in retail, bulk, and services segments. Net income attributable to stockholders was $4.0 million ($0.25 per diluted share), down from $5.2 million in the prior period due primarily to lower manufacturing gross profit and a change in revenue mix. Management noted that full-year 2026 manufacturing results are expected to remain below last year's record level, though they expressed cautious optimism regarding future quarters supported by new orders.

CoreWeave reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.6 billion (up 112% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $128 million with expanding margins. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $12.4B-$13.2B in revenue and $960M-$1.15B in adjusted operating income, while also raising Q3 estimates for both metrics. The company added approximately 500 MW of active power (including a record 300 MW in June) to reach 1.85 GW by year-end.

Ceragon reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $93.9 million (up 14% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.02, driven by strong bookings in India ($120M YTD). Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance but lowered the gross margin outlook to a range of 33.5%-34.5% (from previously implied higher levels) and operating income guidance due to persistent supply chain cost pressures.

Total revenue was $14.9 million in Q2 FY26, down from $15.3 million the prior year quarter and below implied consensus given recent financing news; management raised full-year guidance to a range of $72-76M (back-half weighted) despite missing quarterly targets. Gross margin improved sequentially to 73% driven by higher sales of profitable products following four new regulatory approvals in 2026, while R&D and SG&A declined due to headcount reductions and lower stock-based compensation.

Cardinal Infrastructure Group reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $227 million (up 114% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $28.1 million, though margins were below expectations due to one-time costs, weather impacts in Georgia, and deployment shifts for a diversified project mix. Management raised full-year revenue guidance from the prior range of $680-$890 million to $880-$900 million (midpoint ~$890M) while updating adjusted EBITDA margin expectations to 16%-18% due to transitional costs and SG&A investments. The company also announced the acquisition of Allied Paving, adding $28 million in revenue for Q3.

Net investment income declined to $0.36 per share from the prior quarter's adjusted $0.38 due to lower dividend and realization activity, while NAV fell to $17.82 driven by unrealized losses on non-accrual investments. Management raised concerns about eight consecutive quarters of NAV declines concentrated in a limited set of challenged credits but emphasized progress in rotating legacy assets from over 70 to 27 holdings. The company maintained liquidity with approximately $200 million available borrowing capacity and declared the third quarter dividend at $0.34 per share.

CAVA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365.4 million (up 31.3% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $54.7 million (up 30%), driven by a 9% same-restaurant sales increase on 5.3% traffic growth, though food costs rose 50 bps due to salmon launch input prices. Management reiterated full-year guidance for 75-77 net new openings and mid-single-digit SSS, explicitly incorporating the lingering impact of Cyclospora outbreak concerns which caused same-store sales to dip before recovering sequentially in July.

Broadwind reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of $24.3 million (up 67% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $1.6 million from a loss in the prior year period. Management highlighted record backlog growth across both segments, with Industrial Solutions orders reaching $17.2 million and Gearing orders rising to $16 million. While results were strong on all metrics, management explicitly declined to reinstate guidance pending the completion of their wind tower divestiture scheduled for Q3.

Black Rock Coffee Bar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $63 million (up 25% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 17%, though consolidated earnings were impacted by incremental public company costs. Management raised full-year new store guidance to at least 38 units from 36, citing strong momentum in the California market and a robust pipeline for 2027. The quarter featured same-store sales growth of 4.2% despite lapping a high prior year period.

Brookdale Senior Living reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $122.1 million (up 4.3% YoY) and RevPAR growth of 8.2%, meeting the full-year guidance range but missing occupancy expectations which grew only 230 bps to 82.4%. Management reaffirmed its annual guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($502M-$516M) and RevPAR (8%-9%), noting that Q3 growth will be similar to Q2 before accelerating in Q4 due to disposition timing, while acknowledging a slight occupancy shortfall driven by move-outs.

B&G Foods reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $383.3 million (down 9.7% YoY) and a GAAP loss of $4 million ($0.05/share), though adjusted metrics beat prior year with Adjusted EBITDA rising to $60.4 million on the back of divestitures, acquisitions, and tariff refunds. Management reaffirmed full-year FY26 guidance for net sales between $1.735 billion-$1.775 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $275 million-$290 million despite a challenging industry backdrop involving inflationary pressures in vegetable oil and spices.

Terrestrial Energy reported Q2 FY2026 financial results with no revenue or EPS disclosed as the company operates on a capital-light development model without current commercial operations; cash burn decreased to $6.4 million from $7.9 million in Q1 due to timing variances, though management expects increased spend later in 2026 for site characterization and testing programs.

Bicara Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 results with total operating expenses increasing compared to the prior year quarter due to clinical operations and development costs for its pivotal FORTIFI-HN01 study. The company ended the period with approximately $497 million in cash, providing a runway into the first half of 2029. Management highlighted strong momentum from recent ASCO data but noted that operating expenses are expected to increase quarter-over-quarter through year-end as they prepare for potential commercialization.

Autolus reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $45.7 million, a significant increase from the prior quarter and year-ago period, driven by strong adoption in over 80 U.S. centers and early launch momentum in the UK. Management raised full-year guidance for AUCATZYL to $140-$150 million (from an original range of $120-$135 million) citing improved gross margins that expanded to 55% from Q1's 6%. The company also announced a new strategic financing with Perceptive Advisors providing up to $250 million in notes.

Astronics reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $260 million (up 27% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 19.8%, driven by volume leverage and a one-time tariff refund. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to the range of $1.02 billion-$1.04 billion, crossing the billion-dollar threshold for the first time. The company highlighted strong momentum in aerospace bookings ($306 million) and significant progress on margin improvement levers including pricing adjustments and workforce stability.

Ampco-Pittsburgh reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $102.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9.8 million (margin expanding to 9.5%), representing a significant sequential improvement as the impact from prior U.K. facility closure flows through results. Customer orders surged by approximately 50% year-over-year, with backlog growing substantially to $385.4 million driven by strong demand in Air and Liquid Systems and recovering roll shipments in Forged and Cast Engineered Products. Management expects a significantly stronger second half of the year despite normal seasonal outages.

Cardinal Health reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $63.7 billion (up 6%) and adjusted EPS growth of 40% to $2.91, driven by strong Pharmaceutical volume demand and a one-time $100 million IEEPA tariff refund benefit in the GMPD segment. Management raised fiscal 2027 guidance for enterprise-wide non-GAAP EPS growth to 13%-15%, projecting full-year earnings between $12.40 and $12.60, while reconfirming long-term organic EPS growth of 12%-14%. The company generated $5 billion in adjusted free cash flow for the year and authorized a new $4 billion revolver facility alongside an increased share repurchase program.

Ambiq reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $33.9 million (up ~90% YoY) and non-GAAP gross profit more than doubling to $16M on a margin expansion to 47.2%. Management raised full-year guidance to approximately $135M despite supply constraints, citing accelerating demand for edge AI that exceeds initial forecasts.

Alcon reported Q2 FY26 sales of $2.8 billion, up 7% year-over-year on constant currency, driven by strong performance in surgical equipment (up 25%) and ocular health (up 12%). Management raised its full-year core diluted EPS guidance to a range of 12%-15%, citing the benefit from share repurchases and a $60 million tariff refund. While implantable growth was modest at 1% due to discontinued PowerVision programs, leadership expressed confidence in PanOptix Pro adoption and a robust pipeline including Vivity Pro.

DoubleDown Interactive reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $94.3 million, an increase of approximately 11% year-over-year compared to $84.8 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA reached a record contribution for the quarter at $39.3 million (up 17%), driven by strong social casino growth and improved profitability from direct-to-consumer initiatives, which now account for over half of that segment's revenue. Management maintained its strategic focus on operational excellence and DTC migration while noting sequential flatness in iGaming due to U.K. tax adjustments.

BCSF reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.44 per share and EPS of $0.22, resulting in a NAV decline to $16.65 due to realized losses driven by an exit and restructuring activity. Management maintained the base dividend at $0.42 but declined to provide specific forward guidance on payout levels or ROE targets, citing variables like interest rates and debt maturities as factors for future reevaluation. While credit fundamentals remained healthy with median leverage of 4.7x, non-accruals increased slightly quarter-over-quarter.

EagleRock reported Q2 FY2026 normalized revenue of $46.8 million (up ~32% vs Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $36.2 million (up ~32%), driven by strong brackish water sales, surface use royalties, and resource sales. The company initiated full-year 2026 guidance for normalized adjusted EBITDA between $129M-$133M, which is above original expectations but explicitly excludes the recently announced Intrepid Ranch acquisition. Management highlighted a robust balance sheet with $261.8 million in available liquidity and high free cash flow conversion of approximately 96% after adjusting for interest expense.

Firefly reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $117.7 million (up 46% sequentially and 659% YoY) driven by five parallel lunar missions and strong spacecraft demand. The company closed the quarter with a historic backlog of $1.5 billion, up from $1.3 billion previously. GAAP gross margin declined slightly to 20.3% due to specific government program hardware purchases, while non-GAAP operating loss narrowed significantly as revenue scaled.

IMOS reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue of NT$7,383 million (up 28.7% YoY) and gross margin expanding to 18.0%, driven by record demand exceeding capacity in memory products which grew over 46% year-over-year. Net earnings per ADS reached a new high of $0.80 compared to a loss last year, with management raising CapEx guidance for the full year above 25% of revenue and planning further expansion into AI ASIC testing.

Elbit Systems reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $2.287 billion (up 15.9% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $3.61 (up 34%), driven by double-digit growth across all segments including a record backlog expansion to $32 billion. Gross margins expanded sequentially, with non-GAAP gross margin reaching 25.6%, while operating income grew significantly due to favorable project mix in the U.S. and Israel inventory replenishments. Management highlighted strong demand visibility from Europe and North America, noting that customers are increasingly willing to fund capacity expansion directly.

Imunon reported Q2 FY2026 results with R&D expenses of $1.5 million and G&A expenses down approximately 20% to $1.3 million due to cost containment initiatives. The company highlighted strong enrollment momentum in the pivotal OVATION 3 study, currently enrolling at 0.5 patients per site per month versus a plan assumption of 0.3, exceeding industry benchmarks for ovarian cancer trials. Management confirmed no guidance updates were provided but expressed high confidence that execution remains on track with their target timeline.

IHG reported strong first-half performance with global RevPAR growth of 4.1%, gross system growth of 6.5%, and net system growth of 5%. Adjusted earnings per share grew 13% supported by a record development pipeline where openings and signings were up 8% year-on-year, while fee margins expanded by 120 basis points.

i-80 Gold reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $24 million and a net loss of $53 million ($0.06/share), driven by higher non-cash accounting impacts from financial instrument revaluations, financing costs, and increased pre-development expenses despite gross profit rising to $9 million due to gold price increases and production ramp-up at Granite Creek (8,600 ounces). Management reiterated 2026 guidance for annual output of 30,000-40,000 ounces but noted that growth capital expenditures will be below the prior range due to timing on Lone Tree refurbishment accruals and lower exploration spend. The company remains focused on executing its development plan with a strong balance sheet ($465M cash) while acknowledging moderate delays in drilling campaigns at Archimedes and Mineral Point.

HUYA reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of CNY 1.74 billion (up 11% YoY), driven by a 54% surge in game-related services and advertising to CNY 638 million, while live streaming revenue declined slightly year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 14.7%, narrowing the operating loss to RMB 7 million as higher-margin publishing contributions offset slower core streamer performance. Management raised its share repurchase authorization from $50M-$100M and highlighted strong monetization in their new title, Goose Goose Duck Mobile.

Himalaya Shipping reported a net profit of $24.6 million and EBITDA of $44 million for Q2 FY2026, representing significant year-over-year growth driven by time charter equivalent earnings rising from $28,400 to approximately $50,600 per day. The company declared total cash distributions of $0.59 per share and entered into new index-linked charters at premiums above the Baltic Capesize Index while converting several vessels to fixed rates. Management expressed strong confidence in a robust second half driven by structural ton-mile increases from iron ore and bauxite, noting that Q1 2027 coverage is premature given current curve spreads.

Harrow reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $70.7 million (up 11% YoY and ~60% sequentially) with GAAP gross margins at 71%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $350M-$365M, implying a second-half run rate of approximately $235M-$250M. The quarter was driven by record demand in IHEEZO and VEVYE following business rule changes and PBM coverage wins.

Helios Technologies reported Q2 FY26 sales of $232 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.88, which exceeded the high-end of its prior guidance by $0.05 per share. Gross margin expanded 280 bps to 34.6%, driven by volume growth, mix shifts, operational initiatives, and a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Management raised full-year sales guidance to an implied range of $880-$900 million (up from the prior midpoint) and increased adjusted EBITDA margin expectations for the year.

GrowGeneration reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.2 million (up 5.5% YoY) and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.3 million after returning to profitability in the quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from breakeven to a range of $2-$3 million while reaffirming revenue guidance at $162-$168 million, driven by proprietary brand penetration reaching 40% and cost reductions.

HighPeak Energy reported Q2 FY26 production of approximately 45,500 BOE/d, exceeding the high end of guidance despite accelerating completions which caused some frac-impacted volumes. The company generated $281 million in EBITDAX for H1 and absorbed roughly $55 million in net cash hedge losses while maintaining disciplined capital execution with first-half spending at 60%+ of budget. Management expects meaningful declines in second-half capital spend, positioning the business to generate stronger free cash flow as production remains supported by strong well performance.

Flowco reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $236 million (up 13% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $94 million ($93.9m GAAP), maintaining roughly 40% margins despite a 229 bps margin contraction in production solutions due to Valiant integration costs and higher O&M expenses including lube oil and fuel. Management stated results were within original guidance but explicitly noted that cost pressures will continue into Q3, leading them to reflect these headwinds by lowering their third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA guidance range from the prior $92m-$105m (implied) down to a new range of $92 million-$98 million. The company generated $50 million in free cash flow and declared a one-time special dividend alongside its regular quarterly payout.

Factorial Energy reported Q2 FY2026 operating expenses of $13 million and non-GAAP operating expenses of $14.5 million for the six months ended June 30, which were in line with expectations; capital expenditures totaled $0.6 million for the half-year against a full-year expectation of approximately $13 million. The company announced its first commercial battery order from a U.S. drone manufacturer and achieved an automotive integration milestone with Stellantis, but explicitly stated that it expects to generate its first commercial revenue in 2027.

eToro reported Q2 FY26 net contribution of $229 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $78 million (up 9% YoY), with funded accounts growing 18% to 4.28 million despite a sequential dip in assets under administration due to crypto price declines. The company announced the planned acquisition of TradeZero for up to $230-231 million, which is expected to close in H1 FY27 and strengthen its U.S. presence with futures and options capabilities. Management noted that July KPIs showed a sequential pullback in AUA but expressed confidence that activity will recover as markets stabilize.

Evolv Technology reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.8 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 10.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $180-$185 million from the prior forecast of $175-$180 million, citing strong demand for Gen2 upgrades and multi-product adoption.

Fennec Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 net product sales of $17.1 million, a 78% year-over-year increase from $9.7 million in the prior period. The company achieved its seventh consecutive quarter of growth with record demand and an all-time high for completed infusions in July. Management stated they do not provide formal revenue guidance but expressed confidence that trends seen early in Q3 will sustain momentum through the remainder of 2026.

FutureFuel reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $78.7 million, a 120% increase year-over-year driven by volume growth and pricing improvements across its specialty chemicals and biofuels segments. The company returned to profitability with gross profit of $15 million (up from a loss in the prior period) and adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million versus an annualized run-rate loss previously reported, marking a return to profitable growth for 2026. Management highlighted improved plant reliability, regulatory clarity on biofuels mandates, and elevated input costs as key drivers.

LIF reported a record Q2 with total revenue of $159 million (up 38% YoY) and MAU crossing the 100 million milestone for the first time. The company raised its full-year subscription guidance to $475-$480M while lowering hardware guidance due to strategic pricing shifts, though it reiterated overall revenue and EBITDA outlooks. Management highlighted strong international growth (up 45%) and significant progress in their new advertising business.

Management reported strong execution on strategic priorities including major technical milestones in the U.S. Army Color MicroLED program and new prototype orders for Sentinel FPV drones under the Drone Dominance Program. The company highlighted a path to significant gross margin expansion next year through vertical integration of OLED manufacturing, estimating at least 15 points of improvement. While full-year guidance was not provided today, management expressed high confidence in exceeding previous financial targets driven by volume growth and cost absorption.

Perion reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $98.2 million (down 5% YoY) and Contribution ex-TAC of $42.3 million (down 11% YoY), primarily due to promotional terms used for new account acquisition in Perion One which lowered take rates by 4%. While growth engines like CTV (+56%), Digital Out-of-Home (+45%), and Retail Media (+60%) outpaced the market, management narrowed full-year Contribution ex-TAC guidance ranges while maintaining EBITDA midpoint. Management expressed optimism about H2 normalization of margins as promotional effects fade.

OppFi reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $145 million (up 1.9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.33, missing original expectations due to a deliberate tightening in underwriting and delays in new product launches. Management revised full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue ($600M-$625M), adjusted net income ($115M-$130M), and EPS ($1.34-$1.51) downward, citing a delayed line of credit launch (now targeting September) and LOLA system migration completion pushed back by several months. Despite the near-term miss, executives remain confident in long-term targets to achieve $3 EPS by 2028 following the pending BNC acquisition.

Nu Skin reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $320 million and adjusted EPS near the midpoint of guidance, though full-year outlook was revised lower due to significant non-cash charges including a $79M goodwill impairment. Management pushed back India's formal launch from late 2026 to H1 2027 after refining its business model in that market.

NIU reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 1.44 billion (up 14.7% YoY) and sales volume of 434,000 units (up 24%), driven by a structural shift in China towards electric motorcycles which offset declines in the premium e-bicycle segment. Gross margin contracted to 16%, down from last year's levels due to product mix changes toward lower-margin models, inventory write-offs for international micromobility, and elevated raw material costs. Management provided Q3 revenue guidance of RMB 1.86-2.03 billion (up 10%-20% YoY), maintaining a disciplined stance amidst domestic regulatory headwinds.

NIQ reported Q2 FY26 with organic constant currency revenue growth of 5.8% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 23.3%, exceeding the top end of guidance across all key metrics for five consecutive quarters. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance citing strong demand, AI-native solution adoption (revenue up 34%), and structural efficiency gains from restructuring savings nearing completion. The company highlighted a shift in client conversations to strategic engagements regarding agentic commerce and proprietary data assets.

NESR reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $520.8 million (up 59% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 20.4%. Management highlighted resilience against geopolitical disruptions, citing successful supply chain contingency measures like air freight that cost approximately $4M but ensured zero interruption. The company reaffirmed its path toward a $3 billion revenue run rate via the '3B3' strategy.

GoPro reported Q2 FY2026 results but management explicitly withdrew forward-looking guidance due to an ongoing strategic review process involving a potential sale of the company. The CEO highlighted record subscriber attach rates (69%) and strong product reception for the new MISSION 1 series, while noting that full global distribution is still being rolled out.

N-Able reported Q2 FY2026 ARR of $544 million (up 6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins of 29%, but updated full-year guidance downward due to a new CRO transition, shifting UEM/EDR market dynamics, and near-term headwinds. Management announced plans to reduce total headcount by approximately 6% in the second half of the year to realign resources with high-priority opportunities like data protection and security operations. While demand for core security offerings remains strong, growth is expected to normalize later this year as new product introductions drive expansion.

Kaspi.kz reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 15% and adjusted EBITDA growing by 5%, driven primarily by e-commerce GMV growth of 28% on a constant currency basis. Management highlighted the successful launch of Kasper, an AI shopping assistant in Kazakhstan showing high engagement metrics like rapid response times and conversion rates that outperform traditional search methods. The board context increasing dividends by 18% compared to Q1, reflecting confidence in their financial position despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds from interest rate cycles.

International Seaways reported record adjusted net income of $295 million ($5.91 per share) and record free cash flow of $261 million for Q2 FY2026. Management highlighted a constructive outlook driven by elevated ton-mile demand from geopolitical disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, alongside an aging global fleet requiring renewal. The company reaffirmed its disciplined capital allocation strategy with strong liquidity near $935 million.

Fractyl Health reported a net loss of $25.5 million for Q2 FY2026, an improvement from the prior year's $27.9 million loss driven by reduced operating expenses and lower R&D spending on Revita and Rejuva programs. Management highlighted strong clinical signals with Revita patients maintaining over 80% weight loss at one year versus 46% in the sham arm of the REMAIN-1 study, while cash reserves stand at $47.1 million extending into early 2027.

Management reported a successful transition to an HPC and AI infrastructure company, having exited Bitcoin operations in the U.S. while retaining limited Canadian rigs that are assumed to contribute no cash flow for liquidity forecasting purposes. The CEO highlighted significant progress on permitting across three priority sites (Moses Lake, Sharon, Panther Creek) with commercial interest exceeding available capacity, though Moses Lake guidance was delayed by a couple of months relative to original expectations due to the sequential nature of site execution.

Microvast reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $87.3 million, a decrease of 4.5% YoY driven by a $2.7M tariff refund and lower sales volumes in the U.S. and APAC regions. Gross margin contracted to 29.5%, while operating expenses rose due to increased legal fees and R&D labor costs. Management highlighted progress on Huzhou Phase 3.2 expansion and new solid-state cell milestones but noted that full-scale plant construction remains contingent on securing additional financing.

Management reported significant progress in building a unified AI-native health experience and accelerating growth driven by weight loss therapies and re-accelerating domestic revenue from testosterone offerings. The company highlighted the inclusion of Eucalyptus results (approx $40M) within Q2 figures, noting that while international markets are near break-even, strong US cash flow supports aggressive investment in new categories like peptides and injectable/oral TRT.

MPT reported normalized FFO of $0.15 per share in Q2 FY2026, which was in line with expectations despite mixed results from HSA due to EMR conversion disruptions and delayed supplemental funding. Management announced a comprehensive refinancing extending debt maturities until late 2028, eliminating near-term obligations through secured notes issuance and asset sales. While post-acute operators showed strong growth led by MEDIAN and Ernest Health, behavioral health coverage declined slightly in the U.S. and U.K., with specific liquidity pressures noted for HSA.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Hallador Energy reported a net loss of $15.2 million in Q2 FY2026 compared to prior year income, driven by unit outage costs and high power purchase prices during the maintenance period. Management highlighted significant progress on the Turtle Creek Gas project with equipment shipment expected in September and targeted commercial operations in H2 2028 at a cost below $800 million. The company emphasized its strong forward sales position of approximately $1.6 billion for energy/capacity, excluding third-party coal contracts.

monday.com reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365 million (up 22% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin expansion to 17%. Management highlighted strong AI adoption with ARR doubling quarter-over-quarter, though they lowered full-year guidance due to a workforce reduction impact and lapping prior pricing increases. The company reaffirmed its strategic pivot towards up-market enterprise customers.

Lincoln Educational Services reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue growth of 22.4% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 42.4%, significantly beating expectations. Management reiterated full-year guidance while increasing the capital expenditure outlook to support new campus developments in Suitland, Maryland; Tempe, Arizona; and Hicksville/Rowlett. The company highlighted a robust August start projection driven by high school recruiting improvements and noted that student conversion rates are recovering from Q2 pressures.

QCi reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.6 million (up from $3.7M in Q1 and $61k YoY) driven by photonics sales, while operating expenses surged to $21.8 million due to acquisitions and R&D hiring. Management highlighted commercial milestones including the NeuraWave platform readiness and a Dirac-3 delivery but issued cautious guidance for full-year revenue models, noting potential back-loading of Navy contract funding.

Plug raised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 15%-16% following a Q2 where net revenue grew 9% sequentially and gross margin improved significantly from negative 30.7% last year to approximately break-even. Operating expenses declined by roughly 50% year-over-year, while cash usage dropped 58%, positioning the company for positive EBITDA in Q4 driven by H2 volume growth.

Surgery Partners reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $849 million (up 2.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $125 million, beating expectations to reaffirm full-year guidance despite a sequential decline in YTD margins due to payer mix shifts. Management highlighted strong same-facility growth driven by higher acuity procedures and successful physician recruiting, while announcing the sale of Idaho Falls facilities as a major portfolio optimization step that will simplify operations and reduce capital intensity.

RadNet reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $622.7 million (up 25% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $99.7 million (up 22.7%), driven by strong volume growth in advanced imaging modalities like PET CT (+31%) and MRI/CT, alongside significant Digital Health ARR expansion to over $105M. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow while reaffirming Digital Health targets, citing a 238 bps favorable mix shift toward advanced imaging contributing to an improved segment margin of 16.1%. The company highlighted successful integration of recent acquisitions (Gleamer) with profitability turning positive and plans for further M&A capital deployment.

Riot Platforms announced a decisive step forward in its data center business with the execution of a new lease for 191 MW at Rockdale to a leading frontier AI lab and continued progress on AMD's expansion options. The company highlighted strong liquidity with $1.2 billion total ($666M Bitcoin, $549M cash) funded by watching monthly production rather than issuing equity. Management expressed high confidence in the financing strategy involving Morgan Stanley interim facilities and future investment-grade backstops to fund CapEx.

Surf Air Mobility reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $29.5 million at the high end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA loss within range despite volatile fuel prices and weather disruptions in Hawaii. The company achieved significant milestones including a multi-year enterprise contract with Wheels Up for SurfOS, doubling on-demand private charter revenue year-over-year to $12.1M in Q2 alone, and deploying its safety management system ahead of the FAA schedule. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance while announcing an improvement in adjusted EBITDA loss expectations by approximately 40% due to permanent cost controls.

TCMD reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $85.7 million (up 9% YoY) and gross margin expansion to an adjusted 49%, driven by strong lymphedema growth despite a temporary 7% decline in AffloVest due to DME inventory dynamics. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $360-$366 million, citing continued strength in the core business while anticipating normalization of airway clearance ordering patterns later this year.

Target Hospitality reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue of $86 million and adjusted EBITDA of $18 million, driven by significant growth in the Workforce Hospitality Solutions (WHS) segment which saw a 142% year-over-year increase. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance to total revenue of $410-$420 million and adjusted EBITDA of $85-$95 million, citing accelerated ramp-up of new contracts and operational efficiencies. The company highlighted over 9,000 contracted beds secured since January and a pipeline exceeding 20,000 beds tied to AI data centers and power generation projects.

GCT reported a revenue miss with net revenues decreasing by $0.2 million (18%) to $1 million in Q2 FY26 due to customer deployment timing shifts and lower service revenues. While the company shipped over 5,100 units representing strong sequential growth of approximately 71%, GAAP gross margin was negative for the quarter as product sales did not yet offset costs sufficiently. Management provided a neutral-to-cautious outlook on H2 shipments exceeding H1 but noted that cash burn remains elevated due to prepaid wafer capacity commitments in a tight supply chain environment.

Tonix Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $11 million for Tonmya, representing a 197% quarter-over-quarter increase and nearly tripling first-quarter revenue. Management highlighted strong execution with positive trends in prescriptions (up 100%), new patient starts (+36%), and refills (+207%). The company confirmed the activation of its planned sales-force expansion to be fully implemented by September, supported by recent GPO coverage agreements covering approximately 52 million lives.

Upwork delivered Q2 revenue of $191.7 million at the high end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $64.1 million exceeding expectations due to cost discipline. Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $730-$750 million citing persistent AI automation headwinds, SEO impacts on acquisition, and subdued labor markets. While SMB Business Plus grew GSV by 174% YoY and Enterprise demand remains strong, the company expects further deceleration in Q3-Q4 before potential stabilization.

USA Rare Earth reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of approximately $6 million and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $10.3 million ($0.05 per share), with gross margins impacted by higher raw material input costs. Management highlighted significant progress in building an integrated platform, including the acquisition of Serra Verde, commissioning facilities at Wheat Ridge and Less Common Metals, and securing MOUs covering 2,500 metric tons. The company remains on track to complete its definitive feasibility study for Round Top by year-end but noted that commercial magnet sales are expected only by the end of the current fiscal year.

WBTN reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $338.5 million (down 2.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million, which beat the high end of guidance but was below prior year levels due to increased marketing investments in Korea. Management highlighted strong growth in Korean paid content (+4.3%) and advertising (+11.5%), alongside a new strategic direction involving AI initiatives and an investment in RI Games Holdings for IP adaptations. Q3 2026 revenue guidance remains flat-to-low single-digit (0.7%-3.3% CC), with adjusted EBITDA expected between $0-$5 million.

Powerfleet reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $110.8 million (up 6.4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 19.4%, though GAAP income from operations was flat at $300,000 due to interest expenses. Management revised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance down by approximately $17 million (to a range of $468M-$473M) and adjusted EBITDA down by roughly $11 million primarily due to deliberate capacity reprioritization in South Africa and a late-quarter production constraint delaying ~$3.2M of product shipments.

Mesa Laboratories reported Q1 FY2027 results where the core Biopharmaceutical Development (BPD) franchise grew 5% YoY following a sharp decline in the prior quarter, while Calibration Solutions continued steady growth. However, Sterilization and Disinfection Control (SDC) revenue declined 3.6% due to delivery reliability issues rather than demand weakness, causing management to withhold full-year guidance until November alongside H1 results. The company strengthened its balance sheet by repaying $8.7M in debt, bringing net leverage down to 1.85x.

SPG reported strong Q2 FY26 results with domestic property NOI accelerating to 8.5% and real estate FFO growing 7.9%, driven by leasing demand and acquisitions. Management raised full-year 2026 real estate FFO guidance to $13.20-$13.30 per share, citing robust pipeline and reinvestment in center enhancements despite macro sales uncertainty.

The company reported a significant turnaround with net income improving from a $5.9 million loss to $3.6 million in the prior year period, driven by revenue growth of 22.1% and operating cash flow turning positive at $4.4 million. Management highlighted broad-based improvements including an 18.1% increase in GMV, higher conversion rates, and a new FFL transfer service contributing to take rate expansion. While acknowledging seasonal slowdowns in July and temporary demand shifts due to Virginia legislation, the outlook remains strong with adjusted EBITDA exceeding annualized run-rate goals.

Quantum reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $80.8 million, beating the high end of guidance ($75M +/- $2M) driven by strong demand for ActiveScale and tape solutions despite supply constraints. The company achieved its strongest gross margin in five quarters (39.3%) and generated positive non-GAAP adjusted net income ($4M), marking a turnaround from losses in prior periods due to debt extinguishment charges. Management raised Q2 revenue guidance slightly to $82 million while maintaining cost discipline, though they noted supply chain issues with tape drives remain flat.

Sonida reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with same-store occupancy rising 240 bps YoY to 87.8% and NOI margin expanding 250 bps to 32.6%. The company highlighted clear fundamental momentum following its acquisition of CNL Healthcare Properties, citing efficient top-line growth flowing through profitability despite integration activities.

Seadrill reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with $449M in operating revenues and $144M adjusted EBITDA, exceeding expectations due to higher utilization and day rates on legacy contracts. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue ($1.5B-$1.55B) and EBITDA ($420M-$450M), citing a tightening market with inelastic supply versus increasing demand. The company resumed share repurchases, adding $20M to the program, while noting that visibility on specific rigs like Sevan Louisiana remains limited for H2.

Management highlighted a strong institutional super cycle with ETH appreciating 22% in July and spot ETF inflows outpacing Bitcoin's. The company executed capital allocation by raising $75M via direct offering at a premium to NAV while simultaneously repurchasing shares, demonstrating optionality between equity issuance and buybacks. Strategic investments were made into the Galaxy SharpLink Onchain Yield Fund and ecosystem organizations like EthLabs to drive long-term value.

RUM Group reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $40.4 million (up 61% YoY) following the closure of its Northern Data acquisition and formation of Quake AI. The company issued formal guidance for Q3 2026, expecting revenue between $87M-$93M as it transitions to segment reporting. Management highlighted strong demand momentum with >85% GPU utilization on existing assets and a signed multi-year agreement with Together AI.

Rapid7 reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $210.9 million (down ~1.5% YoY) and total ARR decline to $824M due to non-core product pressure, though it beat EPS guidance with upside operating income margins driven by restructuring savings. Management announced a strategic transformation focusing on core Detection & Response and Exposure Management while cutting non-core lines, projecting an exit margin of ~20%. Guidance for the remainder of 2026 was raised significantly in Q4 due to full realization of restructuring benefits.

Rocket Lab reported a record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $234 million (up ~$90M or 62% YoY) and signed over $1 billion in new contracts across Launch Services ($437M+) and Space Systems ($581M+). The company highlighted the pending acquisition of Iridium Communications to complete its vertical integration strategy, expected to close mid-2027. Management expressed strong confidence in Neutron's readiness for Q4 2026 delivery despite a narrowing launch window.

Getty Images reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $229.1 million, down 2.5% YoY and 4.1% currency neutral, driven by declines in the agency business (-13%) and iStock e-commerce due to search traffic headwinds from AI-generated answers. Management terminated the proposed Shutterstock merger citing regulatory burdens and costs exceeding $100 million, leading to a decision not to provide earnings guidance while focusing on balance sheet optimization and liquidity improvement.

Consolidated net sales increased 27% sequentially and 7% year-over-year to $64 million, driven by record international export growth of 74%. Adjusted EBITDA rose meaningfully to $15.4 million as gross margin expanded nearly 10 percentage points due to a favorable mix shift toward EU GMP certified product from the Delta facilities.

GCM Grosvenor reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with fee-related revenue up 11%, earnings growing 21%, and adjusted net income rising 22% YoY. Fundraising accelerated to $2.3 billion in the quarter, driven by credit ($900M) and infrastructure (25%), bringing H1 fundraising to ~$3.9 billion with a full pipeline expected for the second half. Management highlighted significant unrealized gains from SpaceX investments while noting that ARS performance excluding this single issuer remains robust.

AirSculpt reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $42.9 million, a decrease of 2.5% year-over-year driven by a 1% decline in same-center sales and a 2% drop in average watching price compared to an unusually high prior period. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million (roughly 60-70 bps lower than the implied Q1 margin), reflecting deliberate increases of $5 million in marketing spend for brand building, which raised Customer Acquisition Cost to roughly $3,500 per case from approximately $2,900 last year. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance at the low end and updated adjusted EBITDA outlook to a range of $12-$14 million.

AST SpaceMobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $31.5 million, which was consistent with internal plans and sequential growth driven by commercial gateway deliveries and U.S. government milestones. The company reiterated its full-year 2026 guidance range of $150-$200 million as achievable despite higher operating expenses ($119.1M) and capital expenditures (~$610M). Management highlighted a revenue backlog of approximately $1.3 billion, including new U.S. government contract awards with funded near-term value exceeding $100 million.

APEI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $171.7 million (up 5.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $20.7 million (up 36.8%), both exceeding the high end of prior guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($690M-$698M), net income, adjusted EBITDA, and diluted EPS following the completion of its institutional combination which lifted growth restrictions on Rasmussen University. The company also announced a new AI-enabled student lifecycle platform with Salesforce expected to deliver value in early 2027.

AlTi reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA over $5 million (up 9%), but recorded a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $31 million. The quarter was impacted by an unrealized investment loss of nearly $19 million due to the unwinding of one external manager's fund, which also reduced future revenue contributions. Management highlighted strong organic AUM growth of approximately $700 million and ongoing cost discipline initiatives expected to accelerate in 2027.

Alamar Biosciences reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $29.4 million, an 82% year-over-year increase driven by consumable growth and new instrument placements. Gross margin expanded to a record 60%, while operating expenses rose significantly due to IPO-related costs and strategic investments in R&D and commercial teams. Management provided full-year FY2026 revenue guidance of $116 million-$120 million, reflecting expected annual growth of approximately 59%.

ACV reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $214 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $21 million, which exceeded the high end of guidance despite a challenging dealer wholesale market environment. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue ($845M-$855M) and adjusted EBITDA ($73M-$77M) guidance while noting that OpEx was lowered slightly due to AI efficiencies offsetting margin compression from higher no-reserve sales mix.

Archer reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $5 million (a 213% increase quarter-over-quarter) and adjusted EBITDA loss of $177 million, which met the lower end of guidance. Management announced a major strategic transaction to acquire Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid in exchange for Boeing taking an equity stake, with closing targeted by year-end. While management expressed excitement about this inflection point toward diversification into defense and AI, they explicitly warned that cash burn will remain high during the integration period.

The company reported a Q2 revenue decline of 3.5% due to customer order timing in the Rail segment, though year-to-date sales grew 7.6%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.7% sequentially but rose 19.6% year-over-year driven by strong first-half performance and favorable mix. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance with a second half free cash flow range of $15M-$25M, citing robust backlog conversion expectations.

Accendra Health reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of just over 2% excluding a large commercial payer exit and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $60 million, missing internal expectations due to headwinds in top-line growth, delayed cost reduction timing, and slower collection rate recovery. Management revised the full-year 2026 outlook for revenue to between $2.45 billion and $2.55 billion (down from prior guidance) and adjusted EBITDA to between $300 million and $320 million due to Q2 underperformance that cannot be fully caught up in the remaining five months of 2026.

APC reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $39.8 million (up ~4% YoY) and Discretionary Cash Flow growth of approximately 12%. The company announced the signing of an agreement to acquire U.S. Petroleum Partners, which is expected to add roughly $30 million in annualized adjusted EBITDA upon closing later this year. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA at approximately $156 million and Discretionary Cash Flow at approximately $110 million.

Barrick reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of $0.82 and gold production of 796k ounces (3% above guidance), while meeting cost targets despite a one-time $200M Loulo-Gounkoto payment that reduced free cash flow by 33%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 production and cost guidance, noting strong performance in North America which anchored EBITDA at 61% margins. The company announced an agreement with Newmont valued at approximately $4 billion to resolve disputes and integrate assets like Fourmile.

Total revenue increased 1.2% year-over-year to $55.7 million in Q2 FY26, driven by a massive sequential expansion of the CPG division which surpassed its prior guidance for a run rate between $35-$40 million. However, GAAP net loss widened from -$1.7M to -$4.6M due to high food costs and lease termination charges associated with exiting joint venture restaurants. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $215-$225 million while announcing a non-binding LOI for the sale of restaurant operations.

Consolidated revenue of $977 million beat guidance and grew 4.7% YoY, while Digital Audio Group revenue surged 12.4%. However, Multiplatform Group revenue declined 1.6%, missing the 'flat' guidance due to macroeconomic uncertainty and non-cash marketing expenses. Adjusted EBITDA of $152 million slightly beat the midpoint of its range, driven by strong podcast growth but weighed down by lower political advertising in Q2.

MITT reported Q2 FY2026 earnings with GAAP net income of $9.1 million ($0.29 per share) and EAD of $0.24 per share, fully covering the declared dividend while book value increased to $10 per share. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cherry Hill Mortgage Investment Corporation for approximately 30% cash/70% stock consideration, expected to close in Q4 with annual cost synergies of $7-9 million and pro forma leverage settling at ~2.9x. Management highlighted strong growth in the home equity segment (annualized growth nearly 150%) and expects incremental EAD accretion from resolving legacy commercial loans starting in Q3.

Total operating revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $109.4 million, a decrease of 5.3% year-over-year driven by an 8% decline in units delivered to 580,962 despite a 2.9% increase in revenue per unit. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6 million from $11.3 million last year due to seasonally inflated fuel and driver costs that pressured margins throughout the quarter. Management provided H2 guidance of $350-$370M revenue with 8-9% EBITDA margins, noting these figures are conservative as they do not yet fully incorporate synergies from the announced acquisition of Hansen & Adkins.

Q2 revenue was $386 million (up from $356m in Q2 FY2025), with adjusted EBITDA of $54 million compared to a loss of $17 million last year. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook range to $80-$110 million (midpoint $95M) citing favorable settlements and improved underlying economics, though the core business excluding one-time items generated only ~$9m in Q2.

Playboy Inc reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $31.2 million, an increase of approximately 11% year-over-year to $28.1 million in the prior period. The company swung from a net loss of roughly $7.7 million last year to break-even at the bottom line ($200k) and achieved positive operating income of $3 million. Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $7 million, representing its sixth consecutive quarter of profitability.

Q2 revenue was $32.9 million (up 34% YoY on a GAAP basis but down 23% pro forma), while adjusted cash usage improved to $4 million and the company ended with $96.9 million in cash. Due to broad-based execution challenges, market softness, and lower-than-expected performance across research tools and diagnostics segments, management lowered its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from a range of $169-$174 million to $142-$148 million. Consequently, the company pushed its cash flow breakeven target out to 2027.

Telecom Argentina reported consolidated revenues of over $3.4 billion for the first half of FY26, representing a 23% year-over-year increase in dollars and 16% growth in constant pesos including its acquired subsidiary TMA. Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 35.8%, driven by efficiency initiatives at both Telecom (excluding TMA) which reached 40.5% and the newly consolidated TMA unit reaching 29.3%. Free cash flow generation remained robust, increasing by over $200 million year-over-year to approximately $400 million for the half.

Axsome Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net product revenue of $218 million, a 46% year-over-year increase driven by AUVELITY ($180M) and SUNOSI ($35.8M). The company successfully launched AUVELITY in Alzheimer's disease agitation with new-to-brand prescriptions increasing 126% among patients aged 65+ during the first eight weeks of launch, while SYMBRAVO demand accelerated to a 30% quarter-over-quarter growth rate. Management raised full-year guidance expectations based on these strong commercial metrics and pipeline progress.

Second quarter net sales reached a record $627 million, representing a 101% year-over-year increase driven by robust BASX and AAON brand performance. Gross margin declined to 24.3% from the prior year due to ramping costs at new Memphis capacity, outsourcing levels, and inflationary pressures offsetting volume growth. Management updated its full-year outlook expecting sales growth of 55-60%, with Q4 projected as a high-margin quarter driven by pricing actions embedded in backlog.

BridgeBio reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $243.7 million, a significant increase from the prior year period driven by Attruby net product revenue reaching $222.4 million (up ~$150M YoY). The company successfully advanced three late-stage programs into regulatory review with two receiving priority reviews and no advisory committees planned for BBP-418 or encaleret, while infigratinib received NDA acceptance targeting mid-2027 approval. Management highlighted strong commercial momentum for Attruby as the fastest-growing brand in its space at 23%, supported by new kidney protection data.

Cannae Holdings reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenues of $102 million and expenses of $159 million, including a significant $45 million non-cash impairment charge at the restaurant group. The company executed major capital allocation moves by watching its stake in Watkins for $90 million and Brasada Ranch to eliminate a put right, freeing approximately $47 million in capital while retaining SpaceX shares subject to an 180-day lockup.

Ferguson reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $8.8 billion (up 4.6% YoY) and diluted EPS of $3.39 (up 5.3%), driven by organic growth in non-residential markets despite mixed macro conditions. Management highlighted strong gross margins at 31% and announced an acquisition agreement for FloWorks to expand technical valve capabilities, expecting the deal to be immediately accretive. The company maintained a balanced business mix across residential and commercial segments while returning capital via dividends and share repurchases.

Consolidated revenue surged 126% YoY to $228M driven by a massive 230% jump in the ATS segment ($183M), while the Media segment declined slightly (-1%) and posted an operating loss of $3.3M despite expense discipline. Management raised full-year expectations for Q3/Q4 growth but explicitly warned that Q3 will see sequential revenue declines from the exceptional Q2 peak, citing variability in large client ad spend.

Embraer reported a blowout Q2 FY2026 with record revenue of $2.2 billion (+23% YoY) and deliveries up nearly 7%, driven by strong performance in Executive Aviation (revenue +32%) and Defense & Security (revenue +38%). Management raised full-year adjusted EBIT margin guidance to a range of 10%-10.6% citing an improved business outlook, lower tariffs, and extraordinary tax credits, while maintaining delivery guidance unchanged.

Bakkt reported GAAP net income of $80.8 million and diluted EPS of $1.94 for Q2 FY26, driven by a strong commercial result including the inclusion of payments volume in Total Transacting Volume (TTV) which reached approximately $169 million for the quarter ($410 million H1). Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 TTV target of approximately $2.5 billion and expects to reach adjusted EBITDA break-even during Q4 FY26, citing accelerating execution across Markets, Agent, and Global engines.

Draganfly reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of CAD 2.664 million (up 26% YoY) and gross profit exceeding CAD 533k on product sales over CAD 2.5M, driven by a major exclusive win with IACLEA covering 3,000 campuses and the acquisition of Skip Dynamix for fixed-wing strike capabilities. Management highlighted significant pipeline growth in public safety (Small & Rural Association) and defense contracts including DEVCOM counter-drone systems but noted revenue ramp delays due to rigorous qualification processes and supply chain adjustments.

Dole reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.5 billion (up 2.9% YoY) but adjusted net income fell to $35.1 million from $52.9 million due to higher Fresh Fruit costs and a non-recurring legal charge, resulting in an EPS miss ($0.46 vs prior year). Management maintained full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance at approximately $400 million despite elevated fuel/shipping headwinds linked to Middle East conflict disruptions affecting South Africa. The company highlighted resilience in Diversified Americas and completed the Ecuador port sale for ~$95M proceeds.

DJT reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.7 million (up 92% sequentially) but a net loss of $238 million driven by non-cash mark-to-market losses on Bitcoin and legacy litigation expenses totaling roughly $116.6 million. Management clarified that the TAE merger S-4 filing is pending audit completion with an aim to close by year-end, while pivoting away from direct Crypto.com integration in favor of a marketing agreement for prediction markets.

CRC delivered a solid Q2 FY2026 quarter with net production averaging 149,000 BOE/d and Adjusted EBITDAX of $338 million, driven by strong operational execution and synergy capture. Management highlighted sustainable drilling efficiency gains, including faster time to market in California and improved well productivity exceeding type curves. The company announced the acquisition of Crimson midstream assets for a nominal amount pending CPUC approval, which is expected to strengthen its integrated platform and improve price realizations.

CODI reported Q2 FY2026 with strong double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth across subsidiaries despite a one-time $182M gain from the Sterno divestiture and ongoing Lugano litigation costs. Management maintained its full-year fiscal 2026 total subsidiary adjusted EBITDA guidance of $320-$365 million, citing robust performance in Branded Consumer (up 7.2% net sales) which offset a decline in Industrial segment results driven by Altor challenges and lower volume from a large customer. The company highlighted deleveraging progress with leverage down to 4.8x and plans to return capital efficiently once debt levels approach the target of under 4x.

Viant reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue up 34% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $14.2 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance. CTV spend surged nearly 50%, accounting for over half of total ad spend, driven by new customer acquisition via ViantAI and TVision integration pilots showing significant conversion lifts. Management raised Q3 guidance expectations implicitly through strong commentary on durable growth pipelines despite acknowledging a temporary margin drag from TVision.

Caledonia Mining reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue up 16% to $76M and EBITDA rising 16%, driven by an 18% production increase as the mine accessed higher-grade areas following safety improvements. Management highlighted robust cash flows of $28.4M, a quarterly dividend declaration, and significant progress on exploration at Motapa and Blanket Mine's K-Pits. While unit costs were impacted by one-off items like employee trust distributions and wheeling charges, management expressed confidence in the growth pipeline and strategic funding initiatives.

CEVA reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $29 million (up 13% YoY), driven by a record licensing quarter and sequential royalty growth in wireless connectivity and automotive AI. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 13-15% growth, citing strong H1 execution and the ramping impact of new platform-level agreements including an NPU deal with a major global computing firm.

CECO reported a record-setting Q2 FY2026 with revenue of $285 million (up 54% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $40 million (margin expansion to 14.1%). The company raised its full-year consolidated outlook following the acquisition of Thermon, which contributed one month of results in June. Management highlighted a record backlog exceeding $1.8 billion and strong integration synergies captured within 60 days.

Ceribell reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $28.1 million (33% YoY growth) and a record growth margin of 92%. Management raised the commercial launch timeline for their Delirium solution to Q4 2026, citing positive pilot feedback and new CMS reimbursement rules as key drivers.

Camtek reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $133 million (up 8% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 51.4%. Management raised full-year advanced packaging growth expectations to approximately 70%, driven by strong order intake exceeding $600M YTD, with HBM and CoWoS-like applications leading demand.

Babcock & Wilcox reported a massive Q2 FY2026 beat with revenue surging 130% YoY to $319.7M and adjusted EBITDA rising significantly due to strong Base Electron progress and AI data center demand. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA target range from $80-105 million, citing robust pipeline growth exceeding $14 billion and a backlog increase of over 533% YoY.

Bitdeer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $228.8 million (up 47% YoY) driven by a 377% increase in Bitcoin production and accelerating AI Cloud contributions. The company executed a major strategic milestone with the signing of a $4.7 billion, 16-year colocation lease at Tydal, Norway for NVIDIA GPU infrastructure. Management provided updated full-year CapEx guidance excluding hardware spend ($200M-$280M) while emphasizing progress on project-level financing and operational efficiency.

Ellington Financial reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with GAAP net income of $0.43 per share and adjusted distributable earnings of $0.60 per share, exceeding the dividend. Book value increased and annualized economic return was 13.6%. Longbridge originations rose 38% year-over-year, with record proprietary reverse mortgage volumes and strong securitization execution. The company maintained momentum with portfolio growth, expanding credit hedges, and a pending acquisition, while also enhancing disclosures.

Claritev reported Q2 2026 revenue of $257.5 million, up 6.6% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $155.8 million (60.5% margin), with operating cash flow up 51% to $93 million. Bookings were strong at $30 million ACV in Q2, bringing H1 to $70 million, up 150% YoY, and the company raised its full-year bookings target to $100 million. Guidance was raised, and management expressed confidence in achieving at least 50% ACV bookings growth for the year.

CareTrust REIT reported record Q2 2026 investments of approximately $900 million at a blended 8.9% yield, leading to record revenues, normalized FFO per share of $0.51 (up 19% YoY), and a raised full-year 2026 guidance to $2.03-$2.06 normalized FFO per share. The pipeline remains strong at $540 million with additional investments closed post-quarter, and the balance sheet is highly liquid with net debt to EBITDA at 1.0x. Management expressed strong confidence in continued growth across skilled nursing, SHOP, and U.K. care homes.

Casella Waste Systems reported Q2 2026 revenue of $543.7 million, up 16.9% year-over-year, beating the prior guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $123.2 million, up 12.5% year-over-year, with margin down 80 basis points to 22.7%. Revenue guidance was raised by $30 million, but adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, and operating cash flow guidance were reaffirmed. Management highlighted strong pricing, landfill volume growth, and M&A integration, but noted fuel and resource solutions margin headwinds.

In H1 2026, revenue grew 13.9% YoY to RMB 14.7 billion, with engine unit sales up 10.9%. Gross profit rose 36.5% to RMB 2.5 billion, and operating profit increased 58.9% to RMB 988.2 million. Net profit attributable to shareholders surged 53.2% to RMB 560.6 million. Management noted strong demand for high-horsepower engines, with AI data center sales reaching 1,800 units, and reiterated a full-year AIDC volume target of 3,500 units. The company raised its 2025 dividend to $0.87 per share and is planning capacity expansion to 5,000 units for high-horsepower engines.

Docebo reported Q2 2026 with ARR re-acceleration for the second consecutive quarter, driven by broad-based strength across net new, expansion, and international. Management expressed high confidence in second-half acceleration, supported by lapping AWS and Dayforce headwinds (approx. $19M over next four quarters) and a strong FedRAMP pipeline. The company is investing in a foundational FDE team for agentic workflows and a healthcare vertical, following the prior government playbook. Cash position is $45M with $90M debt, and the SIB is expected to have minimal share tenders at current stock price; no major acquisitions planned in next 12 months.

Dauch reported Q2 2026 sales of $2.96B and adjusted EPS of $0.32, with adjusted EBITDA of $389.6M (13.2% margin). The company raised the low end of full-year guidance for sales to $10.6B-$10.8B and adjusted EBITDA to $1.36B-$1.425B, citing strong first-half performance. Synergies reached $70M run-rate savings, on track for $100M+ by year-end. Management expressed confidence in integration progress and future growth, noting strong demand on key platforms and a $2B quoting pipeline.

DraftKings reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $115 million, exceeding expectations despite customer-friendly sports outcomes and higher customer acquisition spend. Revenue growth was strong with sports handle up 11% YoY and sports consumer volume up 15%, while customer acquisition surged 75% at the best CAC since Q1 2025. The company's predictions offering saw volume grow from $2.3 billion to $11 billion annualized between April and July, with over 600,000 customers engaged. Full-year guidance is maintained at $6.5-$6.9 billion revenue and $700-$900 million adjusted EBITDA, with core business on track for ~$1 billion adjusted EBITDA.

Essent Group reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $190 million or $2.08 per diluted share, up from $1.82 last quarter and $1.93 a year ago, with an annualized ROE of 13.4% and book value per share of $63.01 growing nearly 13% year-over-year. The mortgage insurance in-force grew 1.2% year-over-year to $249.7 billion, persistency was 84%, and the default rate was stable at 2.53%. The reinsurance segment saw net premiums written jump to $249 million in H1 2026 from $31 million in H1 2025, with the combined ratio at 77.9% for the quarter, and management maintained its 2026 P&C written premium guidance of approximately $320 million. Capital returns were strong with $350 million in share repurchases year-to-date and a quarterly dividend of $0.35 per share declared.

VAALCO reported Q2 2026 net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million. Production increased in Gabon to over 9,300 boepd, and Baobab resumed production in June with rates slightly above pre-startup forecast. The company raised full-year production guidance, expanded Egypt drilling to 10-15 wells with no CapEx increase, and maintained CapEx in line with guidance. Management expressed confidence in continued growth into H2 2026 and beyond.

Emera reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of CAD 0.69, down CAD 0.10 year-over-year, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.06, consistent with last year. The company is on track for compound annual adjusted EPS growth above the 5%-7% target through 2026 and within that range through 2030. The New Mexico Gas sale received regulatory approval and is expected to close later this month, with after-tax proceeds of CAD 650-700 million. Management highlighted strong performance at Peoples Gas and progress on data center opportunities in Tampa Electric, while noting lower earnings at New Mexico Gas and higher corporate interest costs.

Concentra reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $606 million, up 10% YoY, with core revenue up 8% excluding acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA grew 22.5% to $140.9 million, with margin expansion of ~240 bps to 23.3%. Adjusted EPS increased ~40% to $0.52. Management raised or reiterated guidance, noted strong organic growth in Onsite Health Clinics, and announced a CEO succession. Leverage fell below 3x, and the company continued buybacks and dividends.

Fidus reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted NII of $0.50 per share, down from $0.62 in Q1, covering the base dividend. Total investment income was $43.5 million, a $4 million decrease quarter-over-quarter due to lower fee income. The company realized $6.4 million in net gains from equity monetizations and exited Virtex non-accrual with a $11 million realized loss, leaving no non-accruals. Management sees deal flow picking up in the second half, citing improved activity levels and a healthy portfolio with 6% EBITDA growth.

Fluor reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 9% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up to $149 million from $96 million and adjusted EPS of $0.91 versus $0.43. New awards exceeded $6 billion, backlog grew to $26.9 billion, and management raised expectations for full-year book-to-bill above 1. The quarter included $44 million in additional losses on the Gordie Howe project, and guidance implies a small step-up in second-half EBITDA, with most of it already in backlog.

Granite Ridge reported Q2 2026 production of 32,044 BOE/d and Adjusted EBITDA of $79.6 million, up from $75.4 million a year ago. GAAP EPS was $0.23, up from $0.19, while adjusted EPS was $0.09. Guidance for full-year LOE was raised to $8.25-$9.25 per BOE, and production is expected to trend toward the lower end of the range. Management reiterated its 2027 free cash flow inflection with strong exit production nearing 40,000 BOE/d and improving gas realizations.

Galiano Gold reported Q2 fiscal 2026 production of 34,400 ounces, bringing first-half output to 69,000 ounces, near the upper end of guidance. Revenue was $156.6 million, adjusted EBITDA $78.5 million, adjusted EPS $0.09, with AISC of $2,473 per ounce, within guidance. Full-year guidance was maintained at 140,000-160,000 ounces and $2,300-$2,600 AISC. The company continued investing in Nkran Cut 3 pre-stripping and exploration at Esaase and Abore, with a planned hedge roll-off and higher-grade ore expected to improve results in 2027 and beyond.

Global Partners reported a strong Q2 2026 with net income of $71 million versus $25.2 million in the prior year, and adjusted EBITDA of $148.2 million versus $98.2 million. Fuel margins improved significantly, and all segments contributed to growth. The company redeemed preferred units at a high cost of capital and maintains strong balance sheet with leverage at 2.85x. Management remains confident in the business despite volatile refined product markets and expects the backwardated curve to increase future inventory carrying costs.

Chesapeake Utilities reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income up 5% and adjusted EPS of $1.05, also up 5% year-over-year (1% EPS increase). The company raised full-year 2026 capital guidance by $100 million to $550-$600 million and announced the $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project. Management reaffirmed long-term growth and expects to provide 2027-2031 capital and earnings guidance in February 2027. Customer growth remains above national averages but showed signs of slowdown.

The E.W. Scripps Company reported a Q2 loss of $12.68 per share driven by a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $1.1 billion and restructuring costs of $36 million. Revenue declined across segments, with Local Media down 1% to $317M due to carriage disputes affecting distribution revenue (-13%) and Networks down 13%. Management raised the annualized run-rate savings target for their transformation plan from prior guidance to $100 million by year-end.

Calumet reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $175 million, with strong performance in both Specialties and Montana Renewables despite planned turnarounds. The company deleveraged below 4x restricted group leverage, repurchased $115 million of notes and terminated a sale-leaseback. Management guided to accelerated deleveraging, announced a novel MaxSAF 150 second-phase expansion to reach 120-150 million gallons of SAF by spring 2027, and identified ~$50 million of low-risk specialty growth capital for 2027-2028.

CGBD reported Q2 2026 NII of $0.35 per share, fully covering the new base dividend, with total investment income of $62 million down from the prior quarter due to lower OID accretion and fee income. NAV per share fell to $15.61 from $15.89, partly due to $24 million in net realized and unrealized losses, including markdowns on SPF and US Infra. Management expects Q2 to be the earnings trough and anticipates increased earnings and supplemental dividends over the next four to six quarters as JVs ramp. Platform originations reached $1.5 billion, up over 20% quarter-over-quarter, but M&A activity remains muted due to geopolitical and macro uncertainty.

GSBD reported Q2 FY2026 NII of $0.38 per share (annualized yield on book value ~12.6%) and NAV of $12.06 per share, down from $12.17. Declared a Q3 base dividend of $0.32 and a supplemental dividend of $0.03, bringing trailing 12-month dividends to $1.54. Net debt-to-equity was 1.35x at quarter end, below target of 1.25x post quarter end, and management plans to reactivate share buybacks. Non-accruals improved to 2.9% (from 3.2%), with a net reduction in non-accrual companies to 10. New commitments were modest at $12.9 million, with a wide spread increase of 511 bps versus six months ago. Management noted subdued M&A activity, but a pickup post quarter end, and remains selective in deployment.

Octave Specialty Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with Insurance Distribution revenue growing 77% to $58.4 million and adjusted EBITDA rising four-fold to $10 million. The company revised its full-year guidance, raising organic growth expectations to 25%+ (from 20%) but lowering total adjusted EBITDA guidance from $40M to $39M ($6M for Everspan) due to higher acquisition costs and interest expense adjustments.

PAGP reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $738 million and raised its full-year guidance to a range of $2.88 billion ±$75 million from the prior implied lower bound, driven by strong crude segment performance ($690M) following an environmental remediation charge in Q1. Management increased 2026 growth capital spending guidance to $400-$450 million and raised Permian production exit-to-exit expectations to 100k-200k bbl/day due to earlier-than-expected gas egress, while maintaining a leverage ratio of 3.3x following the NGL sale.

ACMR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $292.9 million, up 36% YoY, with ECP and advanced packaging growing over 150%. Orders in H1 rose 105% YoY, and the company raised its full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.125-$1.175 billion, implying 25-30% growth. Gross margin was 46% and net cash exceeded $1 billion. The company also announced panel-level plating order wins and progress on PECVD and track platforms.

TDS Telecom delivered 66,000 fiber service addresses in Q2 2026, marking the strongest first-half delivery in company history, and raised full-year fiber address guidance to 250,000-300,000. Residential fiber net adds grew 47% YoY to 15,100. However, total telecom revenues declined 6% (4% ex-divestitures) and adjusted EBITDA was pressured by legacy copper and cable declines, leading to reduced total revenue guidance and narrowed EBITDA guidance. Array's cash site rental revenue rose 65% YoY, and it closed spectrum transactions with T-Mobile and Verizon, while the TDS offer for Array's minority interest remains under review.

Aflac reported adjusted EPS of $1.80 (excluding FX) for Q2 2026, up 1.1% year-over-year, with net EPS of $1.63. Japan sales fell 5.6% in the quarter but were up 7% for the first half, and the company expects full-year Japan sales to exceed 2025. U.S. net earned premiums grew 2.3%, but guidance for 2026 net earned premium growth was lowered to just below the 3%-6% range. Management raised its expected Japan benefit ratio to the high end of the 60%-63% guidance range, due to an unfavorable mix of lapses, and reaffirmed strong capital returns and strategic reinsurance expansion.

Assured Guaranty reported strong Q2 2026 results with adjusted operating income per share up 22% year-over-year to $1.23, driven by higher net earned premiums and lower loss expense. First-half PVP of $152 million was 48% higher than the prior year, led by U.S. public finance and global structured finance. Management remains confident in the pipeline, with $42 million of PVP already expected from Q3 transactions. Record adjusted book value and adjusted operating shareholders' equity per share were achieved.

Q2 FY2026 was exceptionally strong with total portfolio same-store NOI growth of 13.2% year-over-year and 12.7% for the first six months. Same-store occupancy held at 90.7% for Trilogy and SHOP same-store NOI grew 20.5% year-over-year. Management increased full-year guidance and highlighted over $1.4 billion in closed acquisitions year-to-date with $800 million more expected by year-end, none of which is reflected in revised guidance. Net debt to EBITDA stood at 2.5x, indicating continued deleveraging.
